嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖三十五年三月初九日，太子少保、禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣王用賓等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩等六十四員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光祿大夫、柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。
光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太傅、禮部尚書、武英殿大學士徐階〔癸未進士〕。
榮祿大夫、太子太保、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士李本〔壬辰進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Thirty-fifth Year of Jiajing (1556)

The Imperial Voice

On the ninth day of the third month of the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing, your servant Wang Yongbin, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others memorialized at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm, three hundred candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month this year, we should nominate sixty-four officials as readers and other examination functionaries, including Yan Song, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The classes of jinshi status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. By precedent, three candidates shall be selected for the first class: the first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors’ conferred upon them. Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate’; those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the distinction ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Yan Song, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year (1505).〕

Xu Jie, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently serving as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year (1523).〕

Li Ben, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the renchen year (1532).〕

translation_en:
Xu Lun, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Wu Peng, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Fang Dun, Grand Master for Assisting Governance and Minister of Revenue, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

He Ao, Grand Master for Assisting Governance and Minister of Justice, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Zhou Yan, Grand Master for Assisting Governance and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Min Rulin, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, was in charge of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently as Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Lei Li, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Works, was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Zhao Wenhua, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, was in charge of the Office of Transmission and served as Right Vice Minister of Works. He was a metropolitan graduate of the “sichou” year [?; an invalid sexagenary designation in the transcription].

Zhang Shunchen, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Yin Tai, Grand Master of Balanced Obedience, was Junior Supervisor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, in charge of the Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Yuan Wei, Grand Master for Offering Instruction and Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Proctors:

Wang Yongbin, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, served as Minister of Rites and concurrently as Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Wu Shan, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, served as Left Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently as Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Mao Zan, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel, served as Right Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently as Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:

Huo Ji, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Investigating Censor for the Guangxi Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Sun Zhao, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Investigating Censor for the Yunnan Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Script Receiving Officials:

Yan Na, Hanlin Reader, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

In the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing (1556), on the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month, the tribute scholars (gongshi) went to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy questions.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard arranged the imperial ceremonial escort within the vermilion steps and courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the successful candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow announcement of results, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. After the announcement had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month, …

…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a belt were bestowed on the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency on the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of thanks for imperial favor.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Zhu Dashou 諸大綬 was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Duanfu and ranked forty-eighth in his family’s generation. He was thirty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jiong; his grandfather was Hong, a seventh-rank prestige official; his father was Zongjiao; and his mother was née Jin. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Dagang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Daji; Daji, Supervisor in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Dazong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Dayi; and Dajiong. His younger brothers were Dayue, Daxiu, and Dawei. His wife was née Qian. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Dalin 陶大臨 was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Yuchen and ranked thirty-second in his family’s generation. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Huan was honorifically appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs and posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Left Vice Minister of War, and concurrent Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Xie was Left Vice Minister of War and was posthumously granted the title Minister of War. His father Shixian was a student admitted by hereditary privilege, and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dayou, a Prefect; Danian, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; Dashun, a provincial graduate (juren); Dazhuang; Dasheng; Dajie; Dacheng; Daheng; Dayi; Dajin; Dayou; and Dadian. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fourth in both the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Da 金達 was registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Defu and ranked eighteenth in his family’s generation. He was fifty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Haikuo; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Yuxuan; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His first wife was née Ye, and his subsequent wife was née Zhang. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Chen Yang 陳鍚, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fortieth in his family’s birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Xuanping, and his father Yisong; his legal mother was née Weng and his birth mother née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Feng, and his wife was née Jin. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Long 孫鑨, courtesy name Wenzhong, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and came from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twenty-third in his family’s birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Xin was honorifically appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and posthumously honored as Minister of Rites. His grandfather Sui was Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, posthumously honored as Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Zhonglie. His father Sheng was Right Vice Minister of Personnel. His mother, née Han, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother, née Yang, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brothers were Kui, Deputy Office Manager in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Ke, an Imperial University student; Zhen, a tribute scholar; Yu, Vice Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard; and Ao, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Ting, a Hanlin Academy Compiler; Jun; Kuang; and Xiang. His wife was née Qian. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Ke 戴科, courtesy name Chaobin, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in his family’s birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shusheng; his grandfather Yunmian held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father Tingzhang was an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Peng and his stepmother née Guo. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brothers were Mu and Jia, and his wife was née Lin. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Fenglai, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruiyu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Nan, and his father Yin; his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fengyi and Fengling, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Ji, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiyu, his grandfather Yin, and his father Dehou; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xi, Ji 佶, Zhou, Zhan, Lian, Tang, and Lin, and his wife was née Cen. He placed thirteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Dian, registered in a civilian household in Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kecong; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sicheng, his grandfather Yue, and his father Fenglou; his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Xie. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Zichao was registered in a military household of the Xingzhou Rear屯 Guard [Xingzhou Houtun Guard], in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a Sanhe County school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yili; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ding was an Imperial Physician, and his grandfather Kui was a Clerk in the Imperial Medical Academy; his father was Yinglong and his mother née Huang. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Liangfu, and his younger brothers were Zideng, Ziliang, Zixue, and Zibang; his wife was née Hu. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Dayou, courtesy name Yuanjing, was registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanqing; his grandfather, Wei; his father, Shizhu; and his mother, née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Damo, Dahua, Dawu, Dashi, Dalu, Dali, and Dalin; his wife was née Lin. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Menghan, courtesy name Yuwen, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chang (a magistrate, successively granted posthumous honors culminating in Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate); his grandfather, Chun (holder of a prestige title); his father, Kai (an Imperial University student); and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Mei (an Imperial University student), Guangzu (a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites), Guangyu and Guangzuo (both Imperial University students), Guangru, Guangzhai (a commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard), Guangbi (a student admitted by virtue of official family status), and Guangxu (the annotation says “both chiliarchs in the Embroidered-uniform Guard,” but its scope is unclear [?]). His wife was née Zhou. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Ren, courtesy name Qingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. Feng Qian, courtesy name Daoguang, was registered in a military household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rufu; his grandfather, Tingzhi; his father, Wenhuan; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Rang, and his wife was née Dong. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Zhili, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian registration, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingchao; he ranked eighth in the family and was thirty-three years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Yi was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather Hui was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites, additionally granted the posthumous title of Grand Master for Upright Service; his father Bingyi was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhixue (an Imperial University student), Zhiyu, Zhiwen, Zhigao, Zhiqi, Zhihong (an Imperial University student), and Zhilong; his younger brothers were Zhining (an Imperial University student) and Zhiwan. Yuan Sui, registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, under civilian registration, was School Instructor at Jiaozhou, Shandong, specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Minyue; he ranked second in the family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Yingzhao held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Shi (𣐈) [?], his father Huai, and his mother née Song. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Guan, Qian, and Xun; his younger brother was Qian (乾). He married a woman née Xu. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jian, registered in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian registration, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingshou; he ranked sixty-fifth in the family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Hao was a tribute scholar; his grandfather Chang was formerly a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; his father was Mao and his mother née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chan; his younger brothers were Yangtai (an Imperial University student), Yanghui, Yang (鉠), Yangji, Zhen, and Zhi. He married a woman née Du. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Zongming, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian registration, was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked sixth in the family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Hui held an honorary official title for philanthropy; his grandfather was Jing and his father Shou. His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Huang. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Zongwen and Zongbi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Lin and Gao. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

陰武卿〔貫四川成都府內江縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字定夫，行二，年二十九，九月二十三日生〕。曾祖奈，祖璽，父汝夏，母洪氏。慈侍下，兄立卿、文卿，弟惠卿、相卿、定卿、玉卿、長卿、和卿、誠卿，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第一名，會試第二十一名。
translation_en:
Ruan Zisong, courtesy name Weizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Tingzan, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, E, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zidai, Zilun (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Zicen. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Wenhao, courtesy name Guoying, was registered in a military household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather, Wanzhong; his father, Rihua; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenpu and Wenxing; his younger brothers were Wenrong, Wencan, Wenjun, Wenjie, and Wenyao. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Nanjin, courtesy name Zijian, was registered in an artisan household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather, Liangjie; his father, You; and his mother, née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Quan (a County Assistant Magistrate), Xian (a subprefectural Clerk), Yu (a county Clerk), He (a Police Chief), and Jing; his younger brothers were Beiyue, Dongming, and Ximing. His wife was née Yin. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Wuqing, courtesy name Dingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Nai; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Ruxia; and his mother, née Hong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Liqing and Wenqing; his younger brothers were Huiqing, Xiangqing, Dingqing, Yuqing, Changqing, Heqing, and Chengqing. His wife was née Liu. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡孝〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣，軍籍，紹興府餘姚縣人，國子生，治書經，字民行，行一，年三十五，五月二十二日生〕。曾祖瑒，祖尚才，父忠，母沈氏。具慶下，娶余氏，繼娶聞人氏。浙江鄉試第六十七名，會試第一百六十九名。

translation_en:
Wu Yijie 吳一介, courtesy name Yuanshi, was registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuo; his grandfather, Xirui; his father, Tang; his mother, née Jiang; and his stepmother, née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Yibian and his younger brother, Yizhong. He married a woman née Sun. He ranked 104th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Cheng 楊成, courtesy name Ruda, was registered in Changzhou 長洲 County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household, and was a native of Wuxi County, Changzhou 常州 Prefecture. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Qiong; his father, Qiming; and his mother, née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xian. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Lü. He ranked seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xiao 胡孝, courtesy name Minxing, was registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household, and was a native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yang 瑒; his grandfather, Shangcai; his father, Zhong; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Wenren. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Xian 趙賢, courtesy name Liangbi, was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Xing; his father, Xue; his mother, née Zhang; and his stepmother, née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qian, Yue, Ming, Ju, and Zhang; his younger brother was Zan. He married a woman née Lu. He ranked second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄒光祚〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字承卿，行二，年三十五，二月初二日生〕。曾祖廷瑞〔壽官〕，祖魯，父麒，母吳氏。具慶下，弟光裕〔貢士〕、光禎、光祖、光禪、光祜、光袍、光神、光祿、光禴，娶邵氏，繼娶葉氏。江西鄉試第八十四名，會試第一百十三名。
translation_en:
Fang Laichong, registered in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shigong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was apparently twenty-four years old [the age notation is garbled: 二月二十四], born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Feng, Director of Yin-yang Studies; his grandfather was Jie, Steward of Delicacies; his father was Kui, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Yang. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Laixian, a government-school student, Laihe, and Laibin; his wife was née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Jingyu, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhiqing, he ranked fiftieth in the family’s birth order, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongliang, his grandfather Xi, and his father Pei; his father’s former wife was née Ding, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jingkui, a Station Master; Shiqing, a County Registrar; and Jingyi, an Office Clerk [the office is unspecified]. His wife was née Xu. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zongzhen, registered in Dianjiang County, Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University, specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongqi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhiheng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Chao, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zongshi, and his wife was née Hu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Guangzuo, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a county-school student, specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chengqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tingrui, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Lu, his father Qi, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guangyu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Guangzhen, Guangzu, Guangchan, Guanghu, Guangpao, Guangshen, Guanglu, and Guangyue. His wife was née Shao, and his subsequent wife was née Ye. He placed eighty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Zhengmo, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiming; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuhui; his grandfather, Daxing, held an honorary longevity title; his father, Yuanfang, was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Lu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Zhenghe, was a Prefect; his younger brothers were Zhengsi and Zhengyi. His wife was née Hu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Si, registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zirui; he ranked sixty-sixth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Chang, was a Station Master; his father was E; and his mother was née Wen. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Shu, and his younger brother was Lü. His wife was née Yu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Zongchun, registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Renqing; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ning; his grandfather, Yuan, held an honorary longevity title; and his father was Shi. His father's former wife was née Wang, his mother was née Fang, and his stepmother was née Cheng. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Xi, an Imperial University student, Liqing, Zongyan, Zongchang, Zongze, and Zongsheng. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shaoqing, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lei; his grandfather was Xun; and his father, Jian, was a District Magistrate. His legal mother and his birth mother were both née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shaoxin, and his younger brothers were Shaode and Shaozhi. His wife was née Xiang. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡直〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣民籍，應天府六合縣學教諭，治詩經，字正甫，行一，年四十，八月十六日生〕。曾祖爾極，祖行恭，父天鳳，母周氏。慈侍下，弟諒、問、敬，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第九名，會試第十三名。

translation_en:
Bian Weiyuan 邊維垣 was registered in a military household in Peng County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shifu; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian, his grandfather Hong, and his father Zaichao; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weihua and Weifan, and his younger brother was Weiping. His wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ning 王凝 was registered in a civilian household in Yicheng County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, and was originally from Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Di, an Honorary Official for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Cheng, a Police Chief; and his father was Qi, a Department Magistrate. His mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brothers were Zhao and Zhun. His wife was née Liu. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zhi 胡直 was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and served as Instructor at the county government school of Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture. He specialized in the Book of Songs. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Erji, his grandfather Xinggong, and his father Tianfeng; his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Liang, Wen, and Jing. His wife was née Xiao. He placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Guozhen 蔡國珍 was registered in a civilian household in Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Songs. His courtesy name was Rupin; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zhen, and his father 𤐣 [reading uncertain]; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Guoying. His wife was née Xu. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zou Shan 鄒善, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jifu; he ranked twenty-first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sijie, granted the title of Case Reviewer; his grandfather was Xian, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, posthumously granted the title of Grand Master for Governance; and his father was Shouyi, Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yi, a tribute scholar, and Mei; his younger brothers were Yang and Jin. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Gui 黎桂, registered in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kefang; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingwei, his grandfather Qian, his father Dabang, and his mother née Kuang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Keming; his younger brothers were Kejing and Kegong. His wife was née Guo. He placed ninety-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xun 周遜, registered in Maozhou Guard, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to an official household and was a student of the “Chengdu Kui prefectural school” [?], specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Changyan; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged fifty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather was Sheng, a county Registrar; and his father was Wu. His legal mother was née Wang, his stepmother née Zhang, and his birth mother née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Lian; his younger brothers were Shu and Xuan. His wife was née Chang. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiang 張相, registered in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenzhong; he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Xiang, his father Ji, and his mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Qi; his younger brothers were Huan, Chun, Zhen, and Bin. His wife was née Hu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ge Bangdian, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Xuqing, and he ranked third in his family. He was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sichu; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Tan, a School Instructor. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Bangzhi, Bangjiao, and Bangxian, and his younger brother was Bangqiang. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Mei, registered in Yanshan County, Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zihe, and he ranked first in his family. He was aged thirty-nine, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Zi, a District Magistrate; and his father, Xian, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions. His legal mother was née Jiang, and his birth mother was née Qiao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Zhou. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jizhi, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rude, and he ranked tenth in his family. He was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Qin; and his father, Di, a titular official. His mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ji'en, and his wife was née Mao. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Xiying, registered in Ningguo County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chunqing, and he ranked first in his family. He was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiangxing; his grandfather, Yi; and his father, Long. His mother was née Cheng. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Ximin, and his wife was née Yang. He placed 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Renji, registered in a military household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boxiu; he ranked sixth in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Shili, and his father Fu, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under an imperial grace provision. His father's former wife was née Chen, his mother née Niu, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yang and Peng; his younger brothers were Huan, Hao, Yong, Fan, Bangji, and Minji. His wife was née Han. He placed seventieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yipeng, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yingcheng; he ranked thirty-fifth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Huai, and his father Zhi, an Assistant Magistrate; his mother was née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yilong and Yihe, and his younger brother Yifeng. His wife was née Gu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Wenhua, registered in a civilian household in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zibin; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather Qiang was posthumously appointed a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites. His father Shize was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Wenfeng, Wenbing, Wenying, and Wenzhuang. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ji was registered in an official household attached to the Taizhou Defending Battalion in Zhili and was a native of Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Ruji, ranked tenth in his family, and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Lu was an Assistant Instructor, posthumously appointed a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Zuo held an honorary office for longevity. His father, 𤇍 [pronunciation uncertain], was appointed Battalion Commander under a statutory provision; his mother was née Xu. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Mu, Pan, Zao, Xi, Shu, Xun, Zhu, Wen, and Hao; his younger brother was Luo. His wife was née Pan. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Bo, registered in a civilian household in Dianjiang County, Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixing; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Chongyi, was Left Administrator; his father was Zi, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Quan, and his younger brother was Gao. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Qing, registered in a civilian household in Zhangzi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rubi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was Shun; and his father, Ding, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother was née Bao, and his stepmother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Linchen. He married a woman née Song and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed seventeenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingguan, registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingwen; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Chongshi; his grandfather, Guangyin, was an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father, Zan, was a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tinghe, Tingmo, and Tingzhang. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed sixty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xie, registered in an officer household of Lu’an Guard in the directly administered region, was originally from Guangji County, Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunbi; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Hou, grandfather Shi, and father Jie each served as Guard Commander. His mother, née Yang, was granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xun, a National University student, and Gao; his younger brothers were Yong, Ji, Shi, Shi, and Mi. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Qing, registered in a salt-producing household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junfu, he ranked seventeenth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a prefect; his grandfather was Wei; his father was Shangzhong; and his mother was née Zhong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ang, Yi, Bangzhong, Dan, and Bin; his younger brothers were Yu, Lin, Jie, Gao, and Bi. His wife was née Wang. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mengli, registered in a military household in Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruhua, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-four sui, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Xiang; his father was Kun; and his mother was née Gai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chongru, and his wife was née Gong. He placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Lai, registered in a cook household under the Court of Imperial Entertainments and a native of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a Shuntian prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jidong, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-six sui, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuo, an instructor; his grandfather was Wenda; his father was Jin; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuan, and his wife was née Hu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Chaocai, registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shengzhi, he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty-two sui, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoren; his grandfather was Shitai; his father was Hongcan; his father's former wife was née Hong; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chaobin, a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, and Chaoyi and Chaofu, both county magistrates; his younger brothers were Chaos hi [?], Chaohuan, and Chaoshou. His wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Xianshu, courtesy name Huizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Jiajiang County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benxin, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his grandfather was Ziqi, a prefectural vice prefect; and his father was Lu, a student of the Imperial Academy. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Poshu, Yishu (顗淑), Yingshu, Shunshu, and Yishu (頣淑). His wife was née Zou. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Zidao, courtesy name Zifu, was registered in a military household in Pingyuan County, Dezhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial Academy, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Qi; and his father was Kai, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under provisions for imperial favor. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zizhong and Zili, and his younger brothers were Zide and Zixian. His wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yunmou, courtesy name Bangyong, was registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Zhao, a prefect; and his father was Zhang. His mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yun'ao, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tingbao, courtesy name Guoxin, was registered in an artisan-military household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial Academy, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather was Lan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Di, an honorary official recognized for righteousness. His mother was née Sun, and his stepmothers were née Huo and née Wang. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Tingpu, and his wife was née Lü. He placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

項治元〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字熈仲，行二，年三十三，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖忠〔兵部尚書，贈太子太保，謚襄毅〕，祖經〔右參政，進階中奉大夫〕，父錫〔南京光祿寺卿〕，母祝氏〔封恭人〕。慈侍下。兄元淳〔指揮僉事〕、元深〔監生〕，弟元浡、元沐。娶沈氏，繼娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第七十七名，會試第一百九十五名。

葉應春〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字叔華，行八，年二十五，三月二十日生〕。曾祖仁嘵〔壽官〕，祖圓〔散官〕，父統〔縣主簿〕，母俞氏。具慶下。弟應暘〔貢士〕、應時。娶吳氏。順天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百七十名。

凌迪知〔貫浙江湖州府烏程縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字稚德，行一，年二十五，八月初三日生〕。曾祖敷，祖震〔訓導〕，父約言〔知府〕，母潘氏。重慶下。弟述知、遇知、遂知。娶包氏。應天府鄉試第八十九名，會試第一百九十三名。

姚體信〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣竈籍，平湖縣人，府學增廣生，治詩經，字汝達，行一，年二十七，九月初一日生〕。曾祖璋〔贈工部主事〕，祖井〔散官〕，父篹〔監生〕，母陸氏。具慶下。兄一陽、花、體道，弟體仁、體化、儒、仁、德、温、亶、體儉、俊、傑、伊、謙、訓、易、立。娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第八十五名，會試第六十六名。
translation_en:
Xiang Zhiyuan, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xizhong; he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Zhong was Minister of War, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Xiangyi. His grandfather Jing was Right Administration Vice Commissioner, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Central Service. His father Xi was Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing; his mother, née Zhu, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His mother was still living. His elder brothers were Yuanchun, an Assistant Commander, and Yuanshen, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Yuanbo and Yuanmu. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yingchun, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shuhua; he ranked eighth in family order and was aged twenty-five, born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Renxiao held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather Yuan held an unassigned official rank. His father Tong was a County Registrar; his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingyang, a tribute scholar, and Yingshi. He married a woman née Wu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Dizhi, registered in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhide; he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-five, born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather Zhen was an Assistant Instructor; his father Yueyan was a Prefect; his mother was née Pan. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Shuzhi, Yuzhi, and Suizhi. He married a woman née Bao. He placed eighty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Tixin was registered in a salt-producing household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Pinghu County. He was an additional student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruda; he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Zhang was posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather Jing held an unassigned official rank; his father Zhuan [?] was an Imperial University student; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers are listed as Yiyang, Hua, and Tidao [?]; his younger brothers as Tiren, Tihua, Ru, Ren, De, Wen, Dan, Tijian, Jun, Jie, Yi, Qian, Xun, Yi, and Li [?; the division of these names is uncertain]. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xue Yi’e, registered in a salt-producing household in Ruicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yingjian; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zong; his grandfather, Xiong, was a subprefectural judge; his father was Guangpu, and his mother was née Dong. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Yipeng and Yikun, and his younger brother was Yijing. His wife was née Han. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Keda, registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shihong; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jizu, his grandfather was Lian, his father was Wenxiang, and his mother was née Liang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Run, Pei, and Ji; his younger brothers were Kezao, Kejiu, Kemou, and Kexun. His wife was née Liang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Cunxing, registered in a commoner household in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chengzhi; he ranked second in birth order and was aged forty, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Kuang, held the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his father, Dayou, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father’s former wife, née Qin, was posthumously granted the title Lady of the Sixth Rank (anren); his mother, née Peng, was granted the same title; and his stepmother, née Lu, was granted the title Lady of the Fifth Rank (yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cunchu, an Imperial University student, and Cunmo; his younger brothers were Cunxiu, Cunrui, Cunzhuo, Cunsu, Cunyuan, Cunmeng, and Cunzheng. His wife was née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Shoujing, registered in a commoner household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziquan; he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-four, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather was Gang, his father was Neng, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shouyue, and his wife was née Weng. He placed twentieth in an examination whose designation is illegible (□□□試) [?], and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao [?] (高𡹘), courtesy name Shuchong, was registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Zhongxiang County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Jie, a county school instructor; his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Dai, a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and Song; his younger brother was Xue, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Wei. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Feng, courtesy name Yingzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Xingzi County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked thirty-second in family order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Benming, his grandfather Weizheng, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Xu and his stepmother née Cheng. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ren, Bin, and Hui [?] (儶). His wife was née Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Lun, courtesy name Liqing, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changzhou County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was aged forty-two, born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Bai, and his father Chao; his mother was née Shen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Wei and Jin. His wife was née Ling. He placed eighteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Ruqi, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zi, his grandfather Han, and his father Xuan; his mother was née Zou. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ruji and Ruxie. His wife was née Xu. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Chengmin, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shouxi; his grandfather, Maoli; his father, Meicong; and his mother, née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Chengyan, and his younger brothers were Chenghui and Chengyuan. He married a woman née Kong. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lao Kan, courtesy name Renzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Pu, a tribute student posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Fuxiang, a Director in the Ministry of Works granted the additional privilege of wearing fourth-rank official dress; his father was Si; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed ninety-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenyuan, courtesy name Yuanjing, was registered in a military household in Xichong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in family order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jingyuan, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Xiang, a Clerk in a Native Chief’s Office; his father was Tengxiao; and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Li. He placed nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Duchen, courtesy name Dunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather’s name is recorded as 𦭘 [?]; his grandfather was Han; his father was Zongzhou; and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yaochen, a Secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations of the Ministry of Personnel; Jingchen, a provincial graduate (juren); Wuchen, a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; and Shangchen. His younger brother was Wenchen. He married a woman née Du. He placed seventy-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊允〔貫陝西延安府膚施縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字夢鏡，行二，年二十九，四月十八日生〕。曾祖春，祖威〔戶部郎中〕，父本深〔監察御史〕，前母甄氏，母忽氏。慈侍下，兄知、唯吉〔貢士〕，弟栗，娶劉氏。陝西鄉試第十一名，會試第二百九名。

蕭維翰〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字良甫，行一，年三十七，五月初一日生〕。曾祖瑾，祖容，父言〔訓導〕，母張氏。具慶下，弟維寧、維城、維垣、維甸、維宣、維新，娶盛氏，繼娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百六名。

程大賓〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝見，行三，年三十九，九月二十七日生〕。曾祖泰亨，祖倫〔散官〕，父寵，母汪氏。慈侍下，兄大經，娶許氏，繼娶汪氏。應天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百八十八名。

楊侑〔貫四川順慶府南充縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子吉，行三，年三十六，二月初五日生〕。曾祖道達，祖錫，父沐，嫡母馮氏，生母王氏。具慶下，兄儲、仕〔監生〕，弟備、倌、作，娶唐氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第十九名。
translation_en:
Yang Yun 楊允, courtesy name Mengjing, was registered in a civilian household in Fushi County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Wei, was a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Benshen, was an investigating censor. His father’s former wife was née Zhen, and his mother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhi and Weiji, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Li. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Weihan 蕭維翰, courtesy name Liangfu, was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather was Rong; his father, Yan, was an assistant instructor; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weining, Weicheng, Weiyuan, Weidian, Weixuan, and Weixin. He married a woman née Sheng and subsequently a woman née Shen. He ranked fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Dabin 程大賓, courtesy name Rujian, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taiheng; his grandfather, Lun, held titular official rank; his father was Chong; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Dajing. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang You 楊侑, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in a military household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daoda; his grandfather was Xi; and his father was Mu. His principal mother was née Feng, and his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chu and Shi, the latter a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Bei, Guan, and Zuo. He married a woman née Tang. He ranked seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

鮮明瑞〔貫直隸建陽衛官籍，山東東昌府莘縣人，國子生，治詩經，字希文，行二，年三十五，正月初一日生〕。曾祖政〔指揮僉事〕，祖能〔指揮僉事〕，父光〔指揮僉事〕，母蔡氏。慈侍下，兄明道〔武舉〕，弟明初、明善，娶林氏，繼娶施氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第七十八名。
translation_en:
Liu Biao, registered in Ling County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a horse-transport boat household, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaozhong; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather Chong was a county magistrate; his grandfather Hao was a medical official; his father Gongtai was an assistant magistrate; and his mother was née Meng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chaohui and his younger brother Ren. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Min, registered in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a salt-producing household, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shimu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mengyou, his grandfather Luan, his father Hong, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ang, an annual tribute student, and Xu. He married a woman née Lin. He placed sixty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jie Yiqing, registered in Xie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Hua, his father Bin, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yilian and Yizhou. He married a woman née Yi and subsequently a woman née Shi (史). He placed thirty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xian Mingrui, registered in an official household of Jianyang Guard in Zhili and a native of Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiwen; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the first day of the first month. His great-grandfather Zheng, grandfather Neng, and father Guang each served as assistant commander; his mother was née Cai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Mingdao was a military provincial graduate; his younger brothers were Mingchu and Mingshan. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Shi (施). He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□ Daqi (surname illegible [?]), courtesy name Yongqing, was registered in a civilian household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Youxin; his grandfather, Yongti; and his father, Ruluan. His mother was née Qian, and his stepmother was née Duan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dazhen, Dafeng, Dachen, Daning, and Daxi; his younger brothers were Daxian, Damei, Dashun, and Daxiang. His wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuan, courtesy name Minxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xi; his grandfather, Du; and his father, Kuan. His mother was née Zheng. His parents were both deceased. His younger brother was Hui, and his wife was née Li. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengfang, courtesy name Bohui, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing'e, who had been granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Rui; and his father, Wu. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengzhong, an Imperial University student, Chengxun, and Chengye; his younger brothers were Chengqing, Chenggong, Chengde, Chengxu, Chengdu, Chengyong, Chengchong, Cheng'en, Chengzu, Chengyu, Chengzhi, and Chengxiang. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

鮑承蔭〔貫山西潞安府長治縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字子傅，行五，年三十，六月二十六日生〕。曾祖智〔典史〕，祖才〔贈知縣〕，父龍〔前刑部主事〕，母秦氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母秦氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄承恩、承志、承事、承先，弟承訓、承嗣、承業、承芸、承華、承善，娶閻氏。山西鄉試第三十名，會試第二百四十二名。

劉行素〔貫直隸保定府安州高陽縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字易甫，行一，年三十六，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖銘，祖景祥〔封刑部員外郎〕，父恩〔布政司左參議〕，母高氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，弟行可、行簡、行忠、行恕、行義，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第八十名，會試第二百十五名。
translation_en:
Third Class: 203 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Shen Yin, registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingshu; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonglian; his grandfather was Tang, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father was Dajing, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Hong, Chong (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Bin, Wan, Shou, Cai, Cha, and Guan. His wife was née Xu. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 58th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Chengyin, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zifu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, a Chief Clerk; his grandfather was Cai, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his father was Long, formerly a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His mother, née Qin, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of the Seventh Rank; his stepmother, also née Qin, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng’en, Chengzhi, Chengshi, and Chengxian; his younger brothers were Chengxun, Chengsi, Chengye, Chengyun, Chenghua, and Chengshan. His wife was née Yan. He placed thirtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xingsu, registered in a civilian household in Gaoyang County, Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Jingxiang, granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was En, a Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Gao, was granted the title of Lady of the Fifth Rank. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xingke, Xingjian, Xingzhong, Xingshu, and Xingyi. His wife was née Wang. He placed eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.
