translation_en:
Chai Xiang, registered in an artisan household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rujia; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Long; and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhen, and his wife was née Yu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jichun, registered in an artisan household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yingyuan; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-five, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mei; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Donglu; his mother was née Kong; and his stepmother was née Bian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fenchun, Fangchun, and Huachun, and his younger brothers were Maochun and Yichun. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Wenjian, registered in a civilian household in Juye County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tiqian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhou; his grandfather was Jie, a Police Chief; his father was Shuo; his father's former wife was née Zhang; and his mother was née Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Duan and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhuo, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shizhang; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his grandfather was Bi, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father was Guo, a student of the Imperial Academy; his father's former wife was née Tang; and his mother was née Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were En, Can, and Huan, the last a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Tang. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Quan, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chaoming; he was seventh in family order, aged forty, and born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Pu, who held a seventh-rank prestige title. His legal mother was née Zhang and his birth mother née Yao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qin, Director of Food Service, posthumously granted the title of Prefectural Judge; Yue; and Liu, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His younger brother was Xian. He married a woman née Tao. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 93rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Wen, registered in a military household in Zhao’an County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xuanwen; he was seventh in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kemao, his grandfather Hongrui, and his father Qing. His father’s former wife was née Li and his mother née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, Feng, and Gu, and his younger brother was Ye. He married a woman née Deng. He placed 31st in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 24th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Xue, registered in a salt-producing household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiyan; he was seventeenth in family order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Lian, his father Yi, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiusi, Jiu’en, Kun, a District Magistrate, Mengli, Bing, and Siren; his younger brothers were Sili, Chengzhang, and Chengda. He married a woman née Xu. He placed 14th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhiyi, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Keren; he was twenty-fourth in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Lian, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Hong, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works. His father was Tingzhao and his mother née Luo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhiwei, Zhijun, Zhizai, Zhizuo, Zhili, Zhiguan, Zhijian, Zhiqiao, and Zhibao. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Ye. He placed 28th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Kai, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zizheng. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather Lun and father Huai both held honorary official status for longevity; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi; his younger brothers were Wu (an Imperial University student), Qiao, Bin (an Imperial University student), □ [name illegible], Nan, Quan, and Pu. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Chen. He ranked one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lianfang, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yicheng. Eighth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, his grandfather Tingyong, his father Fengqi, and his mother née Lin. His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Guifang. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Fusheng, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yijian. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenliang, his grandfather Liangrui, his father Youfei, and his mother née Zheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Siwen, registered in Meng County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruzhi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Yu, his father Wu, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Tang. Both parents were recorded as living. His younger brother was Sixian. He married a woman née Niu and subsequently women née Wang and née Lian. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Weng Hui, courtesy name Jifang, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangqi, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Fu, also an Assistant Instructor; his father was Dalun, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lan and his younger brother Qu. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yue, courtesy name Zhenbo, was registered in a military household of Laizhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Macheng County, Huguang. A Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Cong, a District Magistrate; his father was Rui, an Honorary Official; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brother’s name is transcribed as 𡸅 [reading uncertain]. He married a woman née Chi. He placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Guangshu, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Xuan, his father Xiu, and his mother née Pan. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Xu. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Tingpin, courtesy name Daoxing, was registered in a medical household in Dao Subprefecture, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyue, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Chen; his father was Dayi; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingshang; his younger brothers were Tingzhi, Tingbiao, Tingxiang, Tingqing, Tingce, Ting’en, Tingsi, Tingzhen, and Tingxian. He married a woman née He. He placed fiftieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉峴〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字仁伯，行二，年四十，七月初八日生〕。曾祖公碩，祖景瞻，父一春，母胡氏。慈侍下，兄峘〔知州〕，弟崐〔貢士〕，娶張氏。江西鄉試第八十二名，會試第一百七十一名。
translation_en:
Chen Jing 陳旌, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Gucheng County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a civilian household. He was an attached student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Documents. First in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Ruwei; his father was Zhiji, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Jin. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Qi 旂, Qi 旗, and Xuan 琁. He married a woman née Su. He ranked 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Shangde 羅尚德, courtesy name Xirong, was a native of Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, registered in a military household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Rang, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Yongzhang; and his mother was née Hao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Feng. He ranked 52nd in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Dalin 孫大霖, courtesy name Ruji, was a native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a salt-producing household. He was a student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Changes. Tenth in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Lun; his father was Youwen; and his mother was née Xu 許. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Dabin, Dayong, Dachuan, and Daxian; his younger brothers were Daqi, Dahuang, and Daguan. He married a woman née Meng and subsequently women née Yu 余 and Xu 徐. He ranked 16th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xian 劉峴, courtesy name Renbo, was a native of Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gongshuo; his grandfather was Jingzhan; his father was Yichun; and his mother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Huan 峘, a Department Magistrate; his younger brother was Kun 崐, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi). He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked 82nd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

王三聘〔貫山西太原府代州，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字起莘，行二，年三十二，八月二十三日生〕。曾祖忠，祖景華，父伝〔驛丞〕，母李氏，繼母白氏。慈侍下，兄汝詔，娶任氏。山西鄉試第十八名，會試第四十四名。

translation_en:
Ma Chutu, registered in Liaozhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yixiang, he was third in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Qin, and his father Zhen, who held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness (yiguan); his mother was née Xu and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Futu and Chengtu, his younger brothers Zhengtu, Xiantu, Zaitu, Jintu, and Chentu, and his wife was née Hao. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Sanxing, registered in Sizhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Xizeng, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Ren, his father Jian, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Sanxi, his younger brother Sanwei, and his wife was née Li. He placed one hundred fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanpin, registered in Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qishen, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Jinghua, and his father Chuan (伝), a Station Master; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Bai. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Ruzhao, and his wife was née Ren. He placed eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yingfeng, registered in Chalingzhou, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shaoheng, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyu, his grandfather Qia, his father Xianxun, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Yingyan, and he married a woman née Deng and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Rufu, courtesy name Weide, was from Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked tenth in family order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zifu; his grandfather, Weichang; and his father, Yongzhong, a county Registrar. His father's principal wife was Lady Zhang, and his birth mother was Lady Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rurui, and his wife was Lady Li. He placed eighty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rukuan, courtesy name Yanfu, was from Wenxi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, registered in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third in family order and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Ying; and his father was Kongxiu, an annual tribute student. His mother was Lady Wang, and his stepmothers were Lady Wang and Lady Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ruzhong, a District Magistrate, and Ruhou; his younger brothers were Ruji, Ruchen, Rushi, Ruqin, Rujing, Rujian, Ruzhan, Ruzhi, and Ruqi. His wife was Lady Yang. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Fengyi, courtesy name Shunqing, was from Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked forty-sixth in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lang; his grandfather, Zhu, an Assistant Instructor; and his father, Ru. His mother was Lady Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fengyang, Fengchi, Fengqi, Fenglai, and Fengju. His wife was Lady Zhao, and he subsequently married Lady Xu. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Rusheng, courtesy name Yiheng, was from Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked fortieth in family order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wanshan; his grandfather, Yichang; and his father, Zhong. His mother was Lady Kang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Ruchang, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Rurong; his younger brother was Ruwang. His wife was Lady Cao. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

潘清亶〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字懋誠，行二十六，年三十五，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖旻〔贈兵部主事〕，祖應〔贈工部員外郎〕，父武錫，母馮氏。永感下，兄清正、清彥、清高、清宦、清祐、清文〔聽選官〕，弟清並、清亮、清章〔監生〕、清學，娶趙氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第二百三十名。

translation_en:
Zhang Xuegu, courtesy name Daofu, was registered in Nangong County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zhi, his father Cen, and his mother née Ma; both parents were living. His elder brother Jigu was a Ceremonial Usher. He married a woman née Bai. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianyu, courtesy name Shujia, was registered in Shenzhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked seventeenth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather Han was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father Wenqian was a County Magistrate. His mother was née Feng and his stepmother née Liu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianyu 天輿, Tianyou, Tianshu, Tianyang, Tianqu, and Tianzuo; his younger brothers were Tianwei, Tianzhi, Tianyi, Tianheng, and Tianyuan. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Wei. He placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Qingdan, courtesy name Maocheng, was registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked twenty-sixth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Min was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War; his grandfather Ying was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works. His father was Wuxi and his mother née Feng; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qingzheng, Qingyan, Qinggao, Qinghuan, Qingyou, and Qingwen, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His younger brothers were Qingbing, Qingliang, Qingzhang, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Qingxue. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Chengxu, courtesy name Shicheng, was registered in Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked twelfth in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather Jin was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Shi and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengen, an Instructor; Chenghua, Left Supervisor of Instruction in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently an Expositor in the Hanlin Academy; Chengfang, a Ceremonial Usher; and Chengxian, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Chengxun, Chengyi, Chengzu, Chengzong, and Chenghan. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently women née Liu and née Wang. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜謙〔貫河南南陽府裕州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子益，行一，年三十五，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖全，祖奉，父文盛，母繆氏，繼母武氏。具慶下，弟誼，娶郭氏。河南鄉試第十四名，會試第二百八十一名。
translation_en:
Lu Zhongdian, courtesy name Rutian, was from Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twelfth in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, a scholar who held no office; his grandfather was Lian; his father was Yaomo, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhongqing, and his wife was née Hu. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Ben, courtesy name Maowen, was from Lingbao County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather was Gong; his father was Zongru, granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and sash under regulations for imperial favor; his mother was née Jian; and his stepmother was née Li. His father alone survived. His younger brother was Shang, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mingrui, courtesy name Zaizhen, was from Luzhou, Sichuan, and registered in a military household. An attached student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao; his grandfather was Shoudao; his father was Yu, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Yang; and his stepmother was née Li. His father alone survived. His elder brother was Fengyi, a Guard Registrar; his younger brothers were Minghe, a Guard Clerk, Mingshi, Mingyang, Mingqiang, Mingqian, and Mingshi. His wife was née Deng. He placed sixty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Qian, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Yuzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, and registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather was Feng; his father was Wensheng; his mother was née Miao; and his stepmother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Guo. He placed fourteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

王尚直〔貫直隸永平府昌黎縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字舉之，行一，年二十九，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖英，祖杰〔贈監察御史〕，父乾，母郭氏。永感下，兄尚質〔聽選官〕、尚志、尚賢〔歲貢生〕，娶白氏。順天府鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百八十五名。
translation_en:
Li Fuxing, courtesy name Naibing, was from Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and registered in a civilian household. An supplementary student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in birth order and was aged forty, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyi; his grandfather, Hou; his father, Jin; and his mother, née Liang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Fushan, Fuxing (復興), Fuchang, Fuliang, and Furen. He married a woman née Lu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Dachuan, courtesy name Changrong, was from Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wende, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Chi, was Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Bian, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Deng, held the conferred title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dalun and Datian, and his younger brother was Daye. He married a woman née Ren. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Yongshou, courtesy name Renfu, was from Yicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and registered in a military household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked fifth in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather, Fang; his father, Dajing; and his mother, née Jia. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongfu, Yongxiang, Yongzhen, and Yongqi. He married a woman née Kan. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shangzhi, courtesy name Juzhi, was from Changli County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Jie, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shangzhi (尚質), an official awaiting selection for appointment; Shangzhi (尚志); and Shangxian, an annual tribute student. He married a woman née Bai. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

包檉芳〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣，民籍，府學增廣生，治書經，字起春，行十二，年二十三，三月二十二日生〕。曾祖鼎〔知府，進階亞中大夫〕，祖憑，父汴〔貢士〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄櫆〔監生〕、柷、栻、楩、檟、槚〔俱監生〕、楙〔生員〕，弟權、植〔歲貢生〕、椿、林、校、森、梧、材〔俱生員〕、柟、梀。娶曹氏。浙江鄉試第四十五名，會試第九十六名。

胡應嘉〔貫直隸淮安府沭陽縣，民籍，府學生，治禮記，字祁禮，行四，年三十三，四月十七日生〕。曾祖綱〔封刑部主事，贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖璉〔戶部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史〕，父效忠〔知縣〕，母佟氏。具慶下，兄應恩〔歲貢生〕、應捷、應徵〔貢士〕，弟應采、應守、應橋。娶徐氏，繼娶朱氏、馬氏。應天府鄉試第三十六名，會試第三十名。

曹一麟〔貫山東青州府安丘縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字伯禮，行二，年三十，六月十四日生〕。曾祖勝〔歲貢生〕，祖光漢〔歲貢生〕，父汝勤〔歲貢生〕，母王氏。重慶下，兄一麒，弟一鳳、一鶴、一鯨、一豸、一介。娶蕭氏。山東鄉試第十一名，會試第七十五名。

蔡完〔貫湖廣黃州府黃陂縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字人備，行二，年三十五，十一月十一日生〕。曾祖彥文，祖繡，父禎，嫡母甘氏，生母梅氏。永感下，兄寀〔歲貢生〕，弟宰。娶丘氏，繼娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第七十八名，會試第九十名。
translation_en:
Bao Chengfang, of Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, came from a civilian-registered household and was an additional student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qichun. Ranked twelfth among his brothers, he was twenty-three years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather Ding was a prefect, advanced in honorary rank to Grand Master of the Second Order (Yazhong dafu); his grandfather was Ping; his father Bian was a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kui, an Imperial University student; Zhu, Shi, Pian, Jia 檟, and Jia 槚, all Imperial University students; and Mao, a government-school student. His younger brothers were Quan; Zhi, an annual tribute student; Chun, Lin, Jiao, Sen, Wu, and Cai, all government-school students; Nan; and Su. He married a woman née Cao. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yingjia, of Shuyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, came from a civilian-registered household and was a prefectural-school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Qili. Ranked fourth among his brothers, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the seventeenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Gang received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Lian was Right Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father Xiaozhong was a county magistrate, and his mother was née Tong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ying’en, an annual tribute student; Yingjie; and Yingzheng, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Yingcai, Yingshou, and Yingqiao. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently married women née Zhu and née Ma. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yilin, of Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, came from a civilian-registered household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boli. Ranked second among his brothers, he was thirty years old and was born on the fourteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Sheng, grandfather Guanghan, and father Ruqin were all annual tribute students; his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yiqi, and his younger brothers were Yifeng, Yihe, Yijing, Yizhi, and Yijie. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Wan, of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, came from a military-registered household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Renbei. Ranked second among his brothers, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yanwen, his grandfather Xiu, and his father Zhen. His legal mother was née Gan, and his birth mother was née Mei. His parents were deceased. His elder brother Cai 寀 was an annual tribute student, and his younger brother was Zai. He married a woman née Qiu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐九德〔貫湖廣長沙府湘潭縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字伯懋，行三，年二十八，九月初六日生〕。曾祖鉉，祖奉〔壽官〕，父篁，母許氏，繼母袁氏、石氏。重慶下，弟九章、九齡、九灋、九賦，娶黃氏。湖廣鄉試第二名，會試第四十五名。

戴廷忞〔貫湖廣辰州衛籍，直隸鎮江府丹徒縣人，沅陵縣學生，治易經，字懋卿，行五，年二十七，正月十七日生〕。曾祖義，祖源〔壽官〕，父宿〔訓導〕，母宋氏。慈侍下，兄廷憲〔貢士〕、廷恩，弟廷懿，娶唐氏。湖廣鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百九十一名。
translation_en:
Lin De, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Youben; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Shuliang, and his father Shiren; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Gao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jindao, registered in a civilian household in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, was a county-school student and specialized in the Book of Changes [?—the transcription reads Book of Odes]. His courtesy name was Zimian; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Yu (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Li (a Director of Food Services); his mother was née Nie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jinke and his younger brother Jindi. He married a woman née Ren. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Jiude, registered in a military household in Xiangtan County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a county-school student and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bomao; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Feng (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Huang; his mother was née Xu, and his successive stepmothers were née Yuan and née Shi. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jiuzhang, Jiuling, Jiufa, and Jiufu. He married a woman née Huang. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Tingmin, registered with the Chenzhou Guard in Huguang and a native of Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Yuanling county school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Maoqing; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Yuan (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Su (an Assistant Instructor); his mother was née Song. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Tingxian (a tribute scholar, gongshi) and Ting'en; his younger brother was Tingyi. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Fu 馮符, courtesy name Xinbo, was registered in an artisan household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an added-quota student at the prefectural school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Huai; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Hu, and his wife was née Zhao. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yiqian 陳一謙, courtesy name Yongyu, was registered in a civilian household in Yulin Subprefecture, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was 𤇍 [reading uncertain], his grandfather Zan, and his father Mao, a district magistrate; his mother was née Quan and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yimo and Yijian, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked sixteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Zhi 襲芝, courtesy name Yingsheng, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Documents. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather’s name is illegible (□□). His grandfather E was posthumously granted the title of commander of a Police Office, and his father Pang held that office. His mother, née Jin, was posthumously granted the title Lady (Ruren); his stepmother, née Zhu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qin, a police chief, Lu, Shen, and Zhu. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Dong 梁棟, courtesy name Bolong, was registered in a military household of the Xi’an Front Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Anding County, Gongchang Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Xian, and his father Jin; his mother was née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His first wife was née Fan, and his subsequent wife was née Guo. He ranked forty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Ruhუai 章汝槐, courtesy name Ziying, was a National University student registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked ninth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shaoyuan, his grandfather Rirang, and his father Wen, a prestige official; his mother was née Wang, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruzhi, a medical official, and his younger brothers were Runan and Ruli; his wife was née Zou. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yongying 李用熒, courtesy name Ruming, was a department school student registered in a military household in Gaotang Department, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong; he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, a department vice magistrate, his grandfather Huai, and his father Qisong, a county magistrate; his mother was née Jia, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Yongbao, and his younger brothers were Yongyao, Yongyi, Yongdeng, Yonghui, Yongguang, Yongzhu, Yonghuang, Yongxie, and Yongbing; his wife was née Liang. He placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Tingzhu 侯廷柱, courtesy name Ziren, was a National University student registered in a civilian household in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked seventh among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tang, who held an honorary title for longevity, his grandfather Yue, and his father Bi, a department magistrate; his father's former wife was née Mao, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Wei, Jue, Tingchen, and Tingxiang, the last a department assistant magistrate; his younger brother was Tingshi, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed fifty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Tingjin 何廷錦, courtesy name Shifu, was a National University student registered in an artisan household in Shaowu County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian; he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather Kuan, and his father Hong; his mother was née Liao and his stepmother née Wu, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingyu, a former investigating censor, Tingxian, a medical official, Tingming, Tingrui, and Tingzhong; his wife was née Gao. He placed 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shang Deheng, courtesy name Rujian, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in the family and was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Tingzhang, and his father Yi; his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dexin, Demei, and Dechun, and his younger brother was Demao. His wife was née Yang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Run, courtesy name Ruoyu, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked ninth in the family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather Diao, and his father Yihe. His legal mother and birth mother were both née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Ying, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed fifty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Zixiu, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangcheng County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-five, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission; his grandfather was Gai; and his father was Jixian, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ziming, a tribute scholar, and his younger brothers were Zimian and Zijing. His wife was née Huang. He placed fiftieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongzhong, courtesy name Ruyi, was registered in a civilian household in Datong County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in the family and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather was Da, Ceremonial Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial, advanced to the prestige title Assistant Gentleman for Court Service; and his father was Shangde, an annual tribute student. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yongbin, a District Magistrate, and his younger brother was Yongyu. His wife was née Guo. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔣弘德〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字宗善，行五，年四十，正月十七日生〕。曾祖福〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖雲漢〔左布政，進階資善大夫〕，父明，母竇氏。慈侍下，兄弘仁〔通判〕、弘義〔知縣〕、弘勳、弘敷、弘儒、弘憲，弟弘烈、弘坤，娶蔡氏，繼娶劉氏。四川鄉試第五十七名，會試第一百五十四名。

translation_en:
Yao Ruxun, registered with the Nanjing Embroidered-Uniform Guard and a native of Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an supplementary student at the Yingtian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xuqing; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-two years old, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Qing, and his father Gao. His mother was née Ran (染) [?], and his stepmother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Chao, registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Darun; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Hongtai, his grandfather Zihao, and his father Wenhui. His mother and stepmother were both née Cai. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Ji, Long, Lian, Han, Zhu, and Chun [division of names uncertain]. His wife was née Shi. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Hongde, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongshan; he ranked fifth in his family and was forty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Fu was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Yunhan was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Fostering Goodness. His father was Ming, and his mother was née Dou. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Hongren, a Prefectural Judge; Hongyi, a District Magistrate; Hongxun; Hongfu; Hongru; and Hongxian. His younger brothers were Honglie and Hongkun. His wife was née Cai; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yanqing, registered with the Muma Battalion and a native of Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student at the Shuntian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shanfu; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yiqing, his grandfather Zi, and his father Long. His father's principal wife and his birth mother were both née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yanfu and Yande. His wife was née Li. He placed ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Yi, registered in a civilian household in Dapu County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenduan; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Feng, his father Boying, and his mother née Luo. His father was deceased and his mother living; his wife was née Qiu. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Shengwu, registered in an official household of Chengtian Guard, Huguang, was originally from Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yisan, ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Hui; his father was Fan, a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Cong. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Dongbi, and his younger brothers were Weiwu, Zongwu, and Jianwu; his wife was née Shen. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ding, registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingzhong; he ranked fifth in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wendao, his grandfather Zhongfu, his father Lian, a County Magistrate, and his mother née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wan, Ning, Xuan, and Kuan, and his younger brothers were Shi, Zong, Shou, and Cai; his wife was née Cai. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Zhi, registered in an official household of Luzhou Guard, Sichuan, was originally from Yutai County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zichun, ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Hu, an honorary official (yiguan); his father was Luan, a Food Service Officer (dianshan); his father's principal wife was née Xu, and his birth mother was née Li. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were En, an Assistant Regional Commander, Mao, Ren, Ai, Wen, Que, and Ci; his wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黎民衷〔貫廣東廣州府從化縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟和，行二，年三十五，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖珪，祖元昌〔封監察御史〕，父貫〔前監察御史〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄民表〔貢士〕，弟民懷、民褒、民襄、民襃、民裳，娶黃氏。廣東鄉試第三十一名，會試第二十六名。

張膽〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州民籍，國子生，治書經，字惟慎，行四，年三十七，六月十三日生〕。曾祖俊，祖昇，父經〔歲貢生〕，嫡母夏氏，繼母王氏，生母陳氏。慈侍下，兄鎰、鈞，弟守中〔貢士〕、守謙、守正、守復、守泰、守乾、同甫，娶丘氏。應天府鄉試第一百六名，會試第一百十五名。
translation_en:
Chen Suoxue, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in an artisan household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather Qian, his father Yanxia, and his mother née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Suojian, and his wife was née Wu. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Daoheng, courtesy name Yufu, was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Wan, his father Yingyuan, his mother née Ping, and his stepmother née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xueshi, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Xuezhong, a Confucian scholar; his younger brothers were Daoning, recorded as holding hereditary status, Daojin, a student of the Directorate of Education, Daolong, Daoming, and Daoyu. His son Tingkai was a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Tang. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Minzhong, courtesy name Weihe, was registered in a military household in Conghua County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather Yuanchang had been granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father Guan was a former Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Li, had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Minbiao was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His younger brothers were Minhuai, Minbao (民褒), Minxiang, Minbao (民襃), and Minshang. His wife was née Huang. He placed thirty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dan, courtesy name Weishen, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Jing, an annual tribute student. His legal mother was née Xia, his stepmother née Wang, and his birth mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yi and Jun; his younger brothers were Shouzhong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Shouqian, Shouzheng, Shoufu, Shoutai, Shouqian (守乾), and Tongfu. His wife was née Qiu. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Biao, registered in a civilian household in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingzhan; he ranked seventh in birth order and was thirty-two years old; his birth month is given as the tenth month [day omitted]. His great-grandfather was Futian, his grandfather Zhongkui, and his father Tianqu. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brother was Kai. He placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xinyi, registered in a military household in Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhunqing; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old; his birth month is given as the second month [day omitted]. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Shangren, and his father Nan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Shu and Shi, and he married Lady Li. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yiji, registered in a military household of Suiyang Guard, Henan, was a native of Wuhe County in Zhili and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianguang; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-nine years old; his birth month is given as the third month [day omitted]. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Shun, and his father Qi; his legal mother was Lady Qiao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yizhu, and he married Lady Zheng. He placed fortieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Yi, registered in a civilian household in Sanhe County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Liangxiang; he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty years old; his birth date is given as the sixth month, tenth day [?; date wording incomplete]. His great-grandfather Sheng was Commissioner of a Tax Office; his grandfather Jingchun held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father Zhitai was a County Vice Magistrate. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, Zuo (an Imperial University student), and You; his younger brother was Fu. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Wenren, registered in a military household of Xining Guard, Shaanxi, was a guard-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiyuan; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather, Jing, was a County Assistant Magistrate; his father, Lai, was a Steward; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Wenda, was an annual tribute student, and his younger brother was Wenming. He married a woman née Li. He ranked forty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Mao, registered in a civilian household of Luzhou, Sichuan, was a native of Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and an attached student at the subprefectural school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zigong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Binrong; his grandfather was Qi; his father, Cheng, was a Steward; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ai, and his younger brothers were Que and Ying. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née He. He ranked forty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Suo, registered in a military household of the Tongshan Defense Battalion under Zhenhai Guard, Fujian, was a native of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, and a guard-school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanwei; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dunjing; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Jingzhan; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lan and Jin. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tingyue, registered in a water-relay-station household of Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yanju; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shigong, was an official awaiting appointment; his grandfather, Xiang, held honorary official status for longevity; his father was Yuanda; and his mother was née Dai. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Tingxi, Tingjing, Tingdui, and Tingquan; his younger brothers were Tinglu and Tingqin. He married a woman née Rao. He ranked twentieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈桂〔貫直隸廬州府無為州，軍籍，浙江湖州府烏程縣人，州學生，治禮記，字仲木，行二，年三十八，三月初十日生〕。曾祖渙，祖安，父璋，前母何氏，母何氏。具慶下，兄椿，弟橋、梓、朴、桐、梗、楫。娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第一百九名，會試第一百六十四名。

陳紀〔貫福建建寧府甌寧縣，軍籍，府學生，治易經，字仲理，行二，年三十，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖善安〔所鎮撫〕，祖仕濂〔所鎮撫〕，父從，母倪氏。具慶下，兄教、焜、煦、炳、文炯、文炤。娶朱氏。福建鄉試第三十四名，會試第五十三名。
translation_en:
Tu Biao, courtesy name Xiwen, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. Fourth in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Xu, and his father Lan; his legal mother was née Shu and his birth mother née Shen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Lian, Commissioner of a capital treasury, and Xuan. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Gu. He ranked twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuan, courtesy name Shuqi, was registered in a civilian household in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tao, his grandfather Yonghou, his father Wandou, and his mother née Xia. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked sixty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Gui, courtesy name Zhongmu, was registered in a military household in Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; his native place was Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Rites. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the tenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather An, and his father Zhang. His father's former wife and his mother were both née He. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chun, and his younger brothers were Qiao, Zi, Pu, Tong, Geng, and Ji. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ji, courtesy name Zhongli, was registered in a military household in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. He was a student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Shan'an and grandfather Shilian were both Battalion Judges; his father was Cong and his mother née Ni. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiao, Kun, Xu, Bing, Wenjiong, and Wenzhao [division of names uncertain]. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Weifu, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Keji, he ranked third in family birth order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Shen, his father Wenqi, and his mother née Li; both parents were living. His elder brother was Weiqian and his younger brothers Weiheng, Weixun, and Weiguan; his wife was née Cui. He placed thirty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shunyue, registered in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Liangqing, he ranked thirty-seventh in family birth order, and he was thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Min, his father Yingkui, his father's former wives née Dong and née Han, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Shunyuan and his younger brothers Shunchen and Shunbin; his wife was née Fan. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Mingfu, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yixiu, he ranked first in family birth order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Shi, his father Zixuan, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongfu, Yangfu, and Laifu; his wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Menghao, registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruxing, he ranked sixth in family birth order, and he was thirty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather Mian held a prestige title; his father Xiyin was a Steward of Food; and his mother was née Liao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Mengxian, and his younger brothers were Mengjie, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Mengcai, Mengji, Mengyan, and Mengzhe; his wife was née Tang. He placed fifth in the Provincial Examination of □□ [place name illegible] and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xia Shi, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Renzheng; he ranked second in family order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zizhen; his grandfather was Fu, an honorary official for longevity; and his father was Chong. His father's former wives were née Ding and née Xu, and his mother was née Shi. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Fang. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Rugui, registered in Jinxiang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Fangfu; he ranked first in family order, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the third day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather was Wen, his father was Dong, and his mother was née Xin. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Ruli and Rushu. He married a woman née Su. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shiqi, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixun; he ranked eighty-sixth in family order, was aged forty-two, and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yu 瑀, his grandfather was Kuang, his father was Yu 玉, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shixiang, Shiyan (a tribute scholar), Shiliang, and Shixie. He married a woman née Bao and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Geng Dingxiang, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zailun; he ranked seventh in family order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyong, his grandfather was Dazhen, his father was Jin, and his mother was née Qin. Both parents were still living. His elder brother was Dingce, and his younger brothers were Dingli 定理, Dingli 定力, and Dingyu. He married a woman née Peng. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖鑑 祖盛〔禮部司務〕 父鶴年〔監生〕 母張氏
慈侍下 弟鈁〔監生〕 鏓 娶葉氏 繼娶陸氏
應天府鄉試第一百十三名 會試第二百六十三名
punctuated:
范以作〔貫四川叙州府富順縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字爾新，行四，年三十五，四月十五日生〕。曾祖弘毅〔助教〕，祖魯，父巡，嫡母劉氏，生母邵氏。永感下，兄汝聰、汝元、以脩、以似、汝恭，弟以佩，娶何氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第一百五十名。

温如璋〔貫河南洛陽中護衛，官籍，山東青州府益都縣，國子生，治易經，字純甫，行三，年三十八，十二月二十日生〕。曾祖厚〔指揮同知〕，祖勝〔指揮同知〕，父新〔戶部主事〕，母王氏。永感下，兄如玉〔指揮同知〕、如春〔評事〕，娶王氏。河南鄉試第七十五名，會試第二百七十八名。

夏可範〔貫江西九江府瑞昌縣，匠籍，國子生，治禮記，字子極，行一，年三十四，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖應冨，祖福泰，父世臣，母王氏。具慶下，弟可畏、可仕，娶曾氏。江西鄉試第四名，會試第二百二十五名。

黃鏓〔貫浙江嘉興守禦千戶所，軍籍，嘉興府嘉興縣，國子生，治書經，字崇文，行一，年三十六，六月初十日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖盛〔禮部司務〕，父鶴年〔監生〕，母張氏。慈侍下，弟鈁〔監生〕、總，娶葉氏，繼娶陸氏。應天府鄉試第一百十三名，會試第二百六十三名。
translation_en:
Fan Yizuo, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Erxin. He ranked fourth in his family, was thirty-five sui, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hongyi, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Lu; and his father was Xun. His father's principal wife was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Shao. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Rucong, Ruyuan, Yixiu, Yisi, and Rugong; his younger brother was Yipei. He married née He. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Ruzhang was registered in an officer household of the Luoyang Central Escort Guard, Henan, and was from Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Chunfu. He ranked third in his family, was thirty-eight sui, and was born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hou and grandfather Sheng were both Vice Commanders; his father Xin was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ruyu, a Vice Commander, and Ruchun, a Case Reviewer. He married née Wang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Kefan, registered in Ruichang County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Ziji. He ranked first in his family, was thirty-four sui, and was born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingfu; his grandfather was Futai; his father was Shichen; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kewei and Keshi. He married née Zeng. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Cong was registered in a military household of the Jiaxing Guarding Battalion, Zhejiang, and was from Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Chongwen. He ranked first in his family, was thirty-six sui, and was born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather Sheng was an Office Manager in the Ministry of Rites; and his father Henian was an Imperial University student. His mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Fang, an Imperial University student, and Zong. He married née Ye and subsequently married née Lu. He placed 113th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳宗周〔貫直隸安慶府懷寧縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字文甫，行一，年三十五，十月十五日生〕。曾祖𤇍，祖綱，父錦，母楊氏。慈侍下，妻劉氏。應天府鄉試第九十七名，會試第一百二十一名。

郜大經〔貫直隸河間府吳橋縣，民籍，山西潞安府陵川縣人，縣學生，治詩經，字汝脩，行一，年三十二，八月初四日生〕。曾祖淮〔壽官〕，祖琛〔歲貢〕，父良臣〔歲貢〕，母杜氏。具慶下，弟大觀、大鯤、大綱、大壯、大綬、大年、大有、大樂，娶周氏，繼娶馮氏、田氏。順天府鄉試第四十名，會試第二百三十五名。

申佐〔貫直隸廣平府永年縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字懋良，行一，年三十四，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖廣〔縣主簿，贈兵部員外郎〕，祖紀〔壽官〕，父成，嫡母魏氏，生母李氏。慈侍下，娶劉氏，繼娶蘇氏。順天府鄉試第一百四名，會試第八十四名。

王道充〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州，民籍，常熟縣人，國子生，治春秋，字懋中，行三，年三十一，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖謹，祖賓〔訓導〕，父法，母陸氏。慈侍下，兄道亨、道玄、道立、道文，弟道章、道齊、道育、道方、道高，娶許氏。應天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百三十二名。
translation_en:
Wu Zongzhou, courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in a civilian household in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was 𤇍 (reading uncertain [?]), his grandfather Gang, his father Jin, and his mother née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Dajing, courtesy name Ruxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Wuqiao County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Lingchuan County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Huai held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather Chen and father Liangchen were annual tribute students. His mother was née Du, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Daguan, Dakun, Dagang, Dazhuang, Dashou, Danian, Dayou, and Dale. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently women née Feng and née Tian. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Zuo, courtesy name Maoliang, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Guang was a County Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of War; his grandfather Ji held an honorary official title for longevity. His father was Cheng, his legal mother née Wei, and his birth mother née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Su. He placed 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Daochong, courtesy name Maozhong, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Changshu County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Bin was an Assistant Instructor, his father was Fa, and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Daoheng, Daoxuan, Daoli, and Daowen; his younger brothers were Daozhang, Daoqi, Daoyu, Daofang, and Daogao. He married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.
