陳應詔〔貫直隸泰州守禦千戶所，官籍，江西吉安府泰和縣人，州學生，治詩經，字仲龍，行二，年三十，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖佐〔壽官〕，祖鸞〔州判官〕，父沐，母周氏。慈侍下，兄應電、應奎、應隆，弟應科、應靈、應爵、應揚、應芳、應旂、應禎、應華、應薦。娶虞氏，繼娶王氏。應天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第四十二名。
translation_en:
Yuan Dacheng, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zongzheng, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was twenty-seven sui, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Longguan, his grandfather Rong, and his father Lin; his mother was née Xia. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Sicheng, a government student, and Zicheng. He married a woman née Tang, and subsequently women née Ying and Chen. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shichang, registered in Gaoling County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongji, and he ranked third in his family. He was twenty-seven sui, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an office commissioner; his grandfather was Kai, and his father Chaoyong; his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shirong and Shihua, and his younger brothers Shiyuan and Shining. He married a woman née Liang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Ruxian, registered in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziguan, and he ranked third in his family. He was twenty-six sui, born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Zongxian, and his father Yi; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shihan, Shimin, Shiqian, and Shijing; his younger brothers were Shishi, Shixi, Shizhe, Shijiao, and Shihua. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yingzhao was registered in an official household of the Taizhou Defending Thousand-household Office in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhonglong, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuo, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Luan, a subprefectural assistant magistrate; his father was Mu, and his mother née Zhou. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Yingdian, Yingkui, and Yinglong; his younger brothers were Yingke, Yingling, Yingjue, Yingyang, Yingfang, Yingqi, Yingzhen, Yinghua, and Yingjian. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Shi, courtesy name Ruxue, was registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Zhen, his father Wenmian, and his mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Huai, He, and Han; his younger brothers were Zhao, Yi, and Li. His wife was née Qi. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiayan, courtesy name Xianke, was registered in Linzi County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Dai, his father Lian, and his mother née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chenyan; his younger brothers were Xunyan and Yongyan. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Feng, courtesy name Tianxi, was registered in Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Xian, a holder of an eighth-rank prestige title. His mother was née Ding and his birth mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui and his younger brother Bi. His wife was née Wei. He placed 101st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Erjie, courtesy name Weifan, was registered in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fiftieth in family order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xifu; his grandfather Yu was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father Pin was a Right Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Erqi, a School Instructor, and Erchang, a National University student; his younger brothers were Erqing, a Secretary, Erke, and Ertong. His wife was née Xu. He placed 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Shunhua, courtesy name Shifu, was registered in a military household of the Lizhou Defense Battalion in Huguang and was a native of Wuling County, Changde Prefecture. An additional-quota student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Hui; and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shunming, and his younger brothers were Shunwen, Shunzhou, and Shunde. His wife was née Qiu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Ou, courtesy name Ruxiang, was registered in a civilian household of Lu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather was Xuan and his father was Yu, both holders of honorary official rank conferred for longevity; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Que, and his younger brothers were Bi, Tai, Ge, and Dian. His wife was née Xie. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Hua, courtesy name Lianfu, was registered in a civilian household of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qing, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Yanling; and his mother was née Si. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shao. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ming, courtesy name Wencui, was registered in a civilian household of Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the seventh day of the intercalary eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, a County Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Ang, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Kejing, a Professor in a princely establishment; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zimian, Zili, Zishan, and Zixin, and his younger brothers were Qi, Yue, and Bin. His wife was née Xiao; he subsequently married a woman née Xu. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Bin, registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziya; he was first in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Jing, and his father Gao; his father's former wife was née Liu, his mother née Lu, and his stepmother née Tu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Cai and Ke, and his wife was née Gao. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ke, registered in a civilian household in Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weijin; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Ji, his father Jia, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhi; his wife was née Pan, and his subsequent wife née Yin. He placed seventy-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Yinglong, registered in a civilian household in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an added-quota student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Bingzhi was a subprefectural assistant judge; his grandfather Yuan held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father was Jingyang. His legal mother was née Chen and his birth mother née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Yinglin and Yingfeng, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Luo, registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuxiu; he was eighth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhen held the titles Grand Master of the Palace and Junior Governor for Aid in Governance and served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate; his grandfather Long held an honorary official rank; his father Yu was a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Zhe, Bian, Bin, Hu, Wei (a subprefectural magistrate), Ji, and Jing; his younger brothers were Qian and Ying. His wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Jiucheng, registered in a civilian household in Chenggu County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zishao; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-one [?; the age marker is missing], and born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Zhu was a county magistrate; his grandfather Yang was a county vice magistrate; his father Zao was a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Fan. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brother was Jiugong, and his wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Zai, registered in a civilian household in Longping County, Zhao Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziheng; he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Chun held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Hu; his father was Ru; and his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Shouyong, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Xiang; his younger brother was Chen. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jianbang, registered in a military household in Guantao County, Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maojin; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Su was a county vice magistrate; his grandfather Yun held an honorary official title for longevity and was posthumously granted the title of county magistrate; his father Dezhi was a subprefect. His mother, née Liu, was invested with the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother was née Guo. His father alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Jiangong and Jianxun, the latter a county registrar. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Xiao. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yongning, registered in a civilian household in Zhangzi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yide; he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather Min was a county vice magistrate; his father was Zongzhou; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brother was Yongkang, and his wife was née Kong. He placed eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Sui, courtesy name Shitian, was registered in Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichang, his grandfather Jing, and his father Yue; his father's former wife was née Xing, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qingyuan, and his wife was née Yu. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Guangjian, courtesy name Yunxian, was registered in Pinggu County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Sheng was a County Magistrate; his grandfather Shu held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his father Rulian was a County School Instructor, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guangyuan, his younger brothers were Guangjiu and Guangxian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Gao, courtesy name Yuanchong, was registered in Pingyuan County, Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in an artisan household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian, his grandfather Zhi, his father Gu, and his mother née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Chen and Zhao, and his wife was née Song. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tonglun, courtesy name Zhongxing, was registered in Hui County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao (昭); his grandfather Zhao (照) was posthumously appointed County Magistrate; and his father Quan was a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His father's principal wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady; his stepmother, née Jiang, was granted the title of Lady; and his birth mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother's name is transcribed as 𡇴 [?], and his younger brothers' names as Cuo, Yu, and Nan (䢐、愚、男) [?]. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Daye 張大業 was registered in an official household of the Dezhou Left Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Yangxin County, Ji’nan Prefecture. An expanded-quota student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuande; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Zan, his father Hong, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Shouye, and his wife was née Bao. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Xi 卞錫 was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shuxiao; he ranked ninth in birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather He and grandfather Xun both held honorary offices awarded for longevity; his father Yu was a county school Instructor, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Ying (a sacrificial official [?]), Kai, Zhu, Zi, Jian, and Ao; his younger brother was Bo. His wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Zeng 薛曽 was registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shikong; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanjing, his grandfather Wenkui, his father Tingxuan, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Da, Qi, and Wei; his younger brothers were Chao and Pu. His wife was née Ye. He placed sixty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Piyang 孫丕揚 was registered in a military household in Fuping County, Yaozhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shuxiao; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Qiong (Commissioner of a Transport Office), his father Weiqian (District Magistrate), and his mother née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Pizhen, and his wife was née Tian. He placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Bai, registered in a civilian household in Shangqiu County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunjie; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Li, and his father Yuan, a prefectural Records Examiner; his mother was née Pei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiao, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Nan; his younger brothers were Ke, Ti, Ji, and Bang. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed fifty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wanyan, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Daoxiang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Mian, his grandfather Qi, and his father Yongyi; his mother was née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Wanxiu, whose annotation reads “shi diantou” (使殿頭) [?]; Wanyan, whose annotation reads “day” (日) [?]; Wanji; Wanyou; Wanbei; and Wanjia. He married a woman née Quan and subsequently a woman née Guan. He placed eighteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chaoyi, registered in a military household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked seventh among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yongxiang, his grandfather Fengwen, and his father Zhongshu; his mother was née Xu and his stepmother née Zhou. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brother was Chaozan. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yangxiang was registered in an officer household of Suiyang Guard, Henan, and was a native of Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Suizhou departmental school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zicun; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Tong, and his father Han, an Instructor in a departmental Confucian school; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yangda, Yanglian, and Yangmeng. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Bangyi, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a military household in Lianzhou, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong; he was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Jing, his father Chao, and his mother née Gao; both parents were living. His elder brother Bangren was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Zhong. He placed forty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Cha, courtesy name Weizhe, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; he was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged twenty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhiyao held an honorary official title for longevity, his grandfather Ju was a School Instructor, his father Wenhan was an annual tribute student, and his mother was née Li; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zun, Cai, and Cong, and his wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zizuo, courtesy name Daohui, was registered in a civilian household in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian; he was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanhan, his grandfather Wenkui, and his father Xuan; his legal mother was née Zhuang and his birth mother née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brother was Zixian, and his wife was née Huang. He placed sixtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shifan, courtesy name Bangzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Lincheng County, Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili); he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Gong was an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang, his grandfather Huang held an honorary official title for longevity, his father was Quan, and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Shifang, and his wife was née Sun. He placed thirty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

何邦禮〔貫福建福州府福清縣鹽籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字大中，行三，年三十三，閏十二月二十五日生〕。曾祖纓，祖文棐，父良贊，母黃氏。具慶下，兄宗魯〔府同知〕、邦麟，弟邦顯、邦紀、邦程，娶方氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第十六名。

許自新〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，府學附學生，治易經，字試可，行一，年二十六，十月十四日生〕。曾祖元興，祖君錫〔貢士〕，父孟春，母傅氏。具慶下，弟知新、維新，娶李氏。福建鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二十三名。
translation_en:
Sun Mengzhi, registered in a medical household in Changyi County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingzhao, he was third in birth order and aged twenty-eight, and he was born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu (honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Yanzheng (honorary official for righteousness), his father Yi (prestige official), and his mother née Song; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Mengqi and Menglin, and his wife was née Liu; he ranked forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Yinghuai, registered in a military household in Hongdong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhiwu, he was first in birth order and aged twenty-four, and he was born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Wei (County Vice Magistrate), his father Chaochen (tribute scholar), and his mother née Zhang; his parents and at least one grandparent were living, his younger brothers were Yinglong, Yingzhao, Yinggeng, Yinglin, Yingluan, and Yingqi, and his wife was née Zheng; he ranked second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Bangli, registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dazhong, he was third in birth order and aged thirty-three, and he was born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Wenfei, his father Liangzan, and his mother née Huang; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Zonglu (Vice Prefect) and Banglin, his younger brothers were Bangxian, Bangji, and Bangcheng, and his wife was née Fang; he ranked twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zixin, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shike, he was first in birth order and aged twenty-six, and he was born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanxing, his grandfather Junxi (tribute scholar), his father Mengchun, and his mother née Fu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Zhixin and Weixin, and his wife was née Li; he ranked fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

錢于鄰〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣，民籍，直隸吳江縣人，國子生，治易經，字震卿，行一，年二十九，正月初九日生〕。曾祖瀚〔義官〕，祖元，父天秩，母沈氏。具慶下，弟于郊、于嘉、于野、于盤、于陸、于石、于陵、于木，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第一百三十七名。

translation_en:
Qi Ruyi, registered in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xingfu, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Xihao, his father Xing, and his mother née Chen; his grandparents and parents were living; his elder brother was Ruqi, his younger brothers were Ruli, Rugeng, and Rubin, and his wife was née Fan; he placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Jing, registered in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Gongzhao, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Feng (an Assistant Instructor), his father Yin (an annual tribute student), and his mother née Lü; both parents were living; his elder brother was Yue, his younger brothers were Dian, Ying, and Jin, and his wife was née Zhao; he placed fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Yulin, registered in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Wujiang County, Zhili; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Zhenqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Han (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), his grandfather Yuan, his father Tianzhi, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yujiao, Yujia, Yuye, Yupan, Yulu, Yushi, Yuling, and Yumu, and his wife was née Wang; he placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Jun, registered in Tang County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Minghe, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Xian, his father Ruzhen, his father's former wife née Li, and his mother née Chen; his mother alone survived; his elder brother was Yong (a County Vice Magistrate), and his wife was née Han; he placed eightieth in the Provincial Examination for □□□□ [place illegible] and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Wei, courtesy name Guozhang, was registered in a civilian household in Mengcheng County, Shouzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zizhong, his grandfather Yue, his father Mengxue, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Chun, and his younger brothers were Luo, Si, Ji, and Wei. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Siyue, courtesy name Zifu, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Dashou, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Chunfan, a Steward; his father was Yizhuang, a tribute student; and his mother was née Chi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Siyin, a tribute student, and Sizhe; his younger brothers were Sidun, Sicheng, and Siyong. His wife was née Cai. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Dahe, courtesy name Daoyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Fen, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; his father was Ti; and his mother was née Xia. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers are listed as Qia, Zhan, and Yuchun, and his younger brothers as Huan, Conglian, Yucheng, Congluo, Lian, and Yuzhi [?]. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Deng. The text then records that Congbian married a woman née Xu [?]. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Chongqian, courtesy name Ruyi, was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yanqi, his grandfather Ao, his father Che, and his mother née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Chong'e, Chongne, Chongrang, and Chongmo. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Shixian, registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guoyong. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Xiang; his father was Yu; and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shitai, Shijun, Shifan, Shida, and Shixian (時憲). He married a woman née Dai and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed forty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qifang, registered in Cheng'an County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jiefu. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiong; his grandfather was Tang; his father was Jing, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Cai. He placed seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Conghuai, registered in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingchang. He ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luwen; his grandfather was Xuan; his father was Pao; and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tiande, a Department Magistrate, and Congwu; his younger brother was Congjia. He married a woman née Huang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yinglei, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an attached student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongfu. He ranked eighth in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather was Han; his father was Dehong; his mother was née Lü; and his stepmother was née Song. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Zongwu and Yingjing; his younger brothers were Yuanli, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Yinglong, Yuanheng, and Yingkui. He married a woman née Lü. He placed eighty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fu Siming, courtesy name Yuanfu, was registered in a military household in Boping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather, Zi; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Sigong (Assistant Prefect) and Sijing; his younger brother was Rumei (tribute student). His wife was née Zhang. He ranked fifty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shunchen, courtesy name Xiren, was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Shangyu County. He was a supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zichang; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Sui (Chief Clerk); and his mother, née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shunmin, Shunzhi, Shunqing, and Shunshang. His wife was née Hu. He ranked nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zhixuan, courtesy name Shunju, was registered in a military household of Wanquan Right Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission, and was a native of Pingyao County, Fenzhou, Shanxi. He was a student of the guard school specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was En; his grandfather, Yue; his father, Mian; and his mother, née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhizhong (District Magistrate) and Zhilian; his younger brother was Zhikui. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shou, courtesy name Huaqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. He was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming (honorarily invested as a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice); his grandfather, Tianfeng (Prefect); his father, Yingqiu; and his mother, née Xiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mi, Yin, Cai, Chen, Qian, Hong, Bin, Kuan, Ding, Huan, and Chong. His wife was née Xiang. He ranked sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Ling, of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Sixing. He ranked thirty-eighth in his family’s birth order and was forty years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tixiang, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Xiyuan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master for Comprehensive Service; his father was Jian, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Quan, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Tong, a student admitted by virtue of official-family privilege; Qian; and Cai, a Subprefectural Judge in Lüzhou [?]. His younger brothers were Hui, a hereditary military cadet of the Yulin Guard [?]; Chuan; Shi; and Ren. His wife was née Li. He placed eighty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Rudi, of Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jifu. He ranked fifth in his family’s birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather was Zi; his father was Jizong, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Rufei, and his younger brothers were Rujian, Ruxuan, Ruzao, and Rudao. He married a woman née Tao and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Shi. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shandao, of Li County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bojing. He ranked second in his family’s birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was Xiu; his father was Bangyou; and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Wangdao. His wife was née Feng. He placed 120th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Zongwu, of Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiyan. He ranked second in his family’s birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather was Youcai; and his father was Jin, a County Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zongdao. His wife was née Gu. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Chaozong, registered in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rubin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Ze, and his father Xiang, a County Registrar; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chaodong and Chaopin. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengshi, registered in Datong County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Ying, his father Man, and his mother née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother Chengbi was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Dong, registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Renfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Jun, his father Shaofang, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Xing and subsequently women née Wang and née Yang. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zan, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingluo [?], he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather Ji was an Assistant Prefect, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Ce and his mother née Lü. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Wan, Qi, Jing, Sui, and Zhang. He married a woman née Miao. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉孝〔貫河南彰德府安陽縣，匠籍，府學生，治書經，字子仁，行二，年三十三，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖廣聰，祖繼宗，父陳殷，母吳氏，繼母郭氏。慈侍下，兄賢，弟真、節，娶張氏。河南鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百四十三名。

translation_en:
Huang Gao 黃誥, courtesy name Rulun, was registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaohong; his grandfather, Zi; his father, Wenchang; and his mother, née Wei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Mo and Xun, and his wife was née Fang. He placed twelfth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang E 黃鶚, courtesy name Zijian, was registered in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather, Xiu; his father, Xiao; and his mother, née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuan, his younger brothers were Ou and Peng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed 131st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xiao 劉孝, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, in an artisan household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangcong; his grandfather, Jizong; his father, Chenyin; his mother, née Wu; and his stepmother, née Guo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xian, his younger brothers were Zhen and Jie, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Yingke 湯應科, courtesy name Tiliang, was registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household, and was a native of Zhangpu County. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongzhi; his grandfather, Hong, was an annual tribute student; his father was Pijun; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tishun, and his wife was née Wu. He placed eighty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Jing, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an supplementary student of the county school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Yinglei, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged forty, born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, an Instructor in a medical school; his grandfather was Zheng; his father was Wenshi; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Feng, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Jing (䲔); his younger brothers were Li, Peng, Kun, Ao, He, and Yan. His wife was née Fei. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Zhu, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the prefectural school; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Luchuan, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather was Xi; his father was Tinglan, granted the honorary title of Right Rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review; and his mother was née Xie, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai, a Left Administration Vice Commissioner, Ze, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Jin, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Yan and An. His wife was née Zuo. He placed thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Jun’en, registered in Qinshui County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school; he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, had the courtesy name Yuanchong, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, a student of the Imperial University; his grandfather’s name is transcribed as 𨺢 [?]; his father was Yongshi; and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Junxiang and Junmo. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Jie, registered in Yuzhou, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school; he specialized in the Book of Rites, had the courtesy name Yanfu, ranked ninth among his brothers, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Wenda, a County Magistrate; his father was Ming, an Investigating Censor; his father’s former wife was née Wang, posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); and his mother was née Li, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouren, Shouyi, Shouli, Shouzhi, Shouxue, Shoucong, Shouyuan, and Ben. His wife was née Wu. He placed tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cheng Chun 程純, registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Guang Zhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zijian, his grandfather Min, and his father Yao; his father's principal wife was née Xiang, and his birth mother was née Ren. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Lun, and he married a woman née Luo. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shipei 張士佩, registered in a military household in Hancheng County, Tong Zhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Meifu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Cui, his father Mengde, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiheng, and he married a woman née Xu. He placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhonghan 陳忠翰, registered in a civilian household in Pu Zhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Siyi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Tong, who held an honorary longevity rank (shouguan), his father Lun, and his mother née Xing. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongjian and Zhongjin, and his younger brother was Zhongli. He married a woman née Hao. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Leiting 楊雷廷, registered in a civilian household in Shunyi County, Changping Zhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziwei; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Yu, and his father Cong; his father's principal wife and his birth mother were both née Zhang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Xin. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Siyi, an official of yin-yang studies; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Zhi, granted the cap and girdle of official status by imperial favor under established provisions; and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yaoxiang, registered in a civilian household in Ruzhou, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongshun; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xiu; his grandfather was Liang; his father was Dao; his mother was née Hou; and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yaochen, Yaoqing, Yaobin, Yaoming (student status unclear: 壙生 [?]), and Yaoshi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fiftieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shouzhen, registered in a civilian household in Gucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Congzheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Delin; his grandfather was He; his father was Jin; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Yan and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 219th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Zhong, registered in a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wanzhong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ziqian; his grandfather was Tang; his father was Kai; and his mother was née Ma. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zhen and his younger brother was Qian. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Huang, registered in a civilian household in Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daohan; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shan; his grandfather was Zhigao, an honorary official appointed in recognition of longevity; his father was Siqi; and his mother was née Liu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Bing and Wei, and his wife was née Fu. He placed fifty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Dajing, registered in a civilian household in Xi’an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhengzhi; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Huai, his grandfather Kui, his father Quan, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xu. He placed twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Guan, registered in a military household in Yicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bingheng; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather was Zan; his father was Quan, a seventh-rank prestige official; and his mother was née Chang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zaidao and Chen, the latter a Subprefect; his younger brother was Shu. His wife was née Guo, and he subsequently married a woman née Lü. He placed fifty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Xiao, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanxue; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather Cheng, grandfather Zhen, and father Zhi had each been granted the title General of Military Strategy. His father’s former wife, née Hu, had been posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Hong, had been granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Xiang was a Vice Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his younger brother was Tang. His wife was née Lin. He placed ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Shouting, registered in a civilian household in Linying County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chunfu, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five [?]; he was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun; his grandfather, Wen; and his father, Cheng, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Du. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shoudu, and his younger brother was Shouyu. His wife was née Zhao. He ranked twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Youcheng, registered in a military household in Ningxiang County, Shizhou Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Cunfu, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven; he was born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichang; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Xizhou. His mother was née Bai. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Youheng. His wife was née Zheng; his subsequent wife was née Cao. He ranked sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yue, registered in a military household in Qianjiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weiqing, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine; he was born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, a Guard Office Manager; his grandfather was Zan, an Erudite of the Nanjing Imperial University; and his father was Gongming, a Subprefect. His father's former wife was née Li, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Neng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Lei; his subsequent wife was née Wang. He ranked ninetieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Fengjie, registered in a civilian household in Gushi County, Guangzhou Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and a native of Guangshan County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yingshi, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four; he was born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Congzheng; and his father, Feng. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmothers were née Cui and née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fengji and Fenghua. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Fumin, registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and originally from Le’an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xizhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Quan, his father Yi, and his mother née Pei. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yumin, Jimin, and Huimin, and his wife was née Yang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Xin, of a military household in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dexin; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhigao, his grandfather Yongkang, and his father Ren, a National University student. His father’s former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née He. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother is recorded as Cai Mao [?], a tribute scholar. His wife was née Jiang; he subsequently married a woman née Zheng. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shida, of a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an added-quota student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, his grandfather Nai, his father Tingxiang, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shiyuan, Shikui, and Shike, and his wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shijian, of a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an attached student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bohong; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sui; his grandfather Hai was Deputy Commissioner of a Tax Office [?]; and his father Yong was a County Vice Magistrate, granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works. His father’s former wife, née Ma, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Liu, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Shiji was a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and his wife was née Kong. He placed seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟
天命立君以宰於率
土必有分理協助
之臣所謂鄰哉也
吁堯舜之克聖不
===
===
有高賢大良之助
豈二聖獨勞耶夫
以古之元首股肱
眞是一體上下相
資不若茲時之大

吁咈之克聖不
===

豈二聖獨勞耶夫
以古之元首股肱
真是一體上下相
資不若茲時之大
punctuated: 皇帝制曰：「朕惟天命立君，以宰於率土，必有分理協助之臣，所謂鄰哉也。吁！堯舜之克聖，不有高賢大良之助，豈二聖獨勞耶？夫以古之元首股肱，眞是一體，上下相資，不若茲時之大
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: “I reflect that Heaven appoints a ruler to govern all the land; he must have ministers who share the work of government and assist him—those called his ‘close companions.’ Ah! In Yao and Shun’s attainment of sagehood, did they not have the assistance of eminently worthy and exceptionally able men? Could the two sages have labored alone? In antiquity, the sovereign as the head and his ministers as the limbs truly formed one body, those above and below supporting one another, unlike the great … of the present age.”

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
不同者朕以心腹
置人心腹中何乃
視我仇讎焉安望
爲國恤民也朕固
無知人之哲能官
===
之智我欲聞是知
能之方尔多士目
覩既眞當有益我
知能之道悉著以
對勿諱勿欺
alt_text:

之智我欲聞是知
能之方尒多士目
覩既真當有益我
知能之道悉著以
對勿諱勿欺
punctuated: 不同者，朕以心腹置人心腹中，何乃視我仇讎焉？安望爲國恤民也？朕固無知人之哲、能官之智。我欲聞是知能之方，尔多士目覩既眞，當有益我知能之道，悉著以對，勿諱勿欺。
translation_en: …the difference is this: I place my own heart within the hearts of others; why, then, do they regard me as an enemy? How can I expect them to care for the people on behalf of the state? I admittedly lack the discernment to judge men and the wisdom to appoint them to suitable offices. I wish to hear how to acquire these abilities. You assembled scholars have seen the situation clearly with your own eyes and should have ways to improve my discernment and ability to make appointments. Set them all down in your answers; conceal nothing and do not deceive me.

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
臣諸大綬
臣對臣聞帝王之致治於無疆也必君臣相
孚而後成德業之盛必仁義相濟而後得馭
臣之方何者君猶天也臣猶四時五行也天
道有默運之神而所以普生成之功者未始
不由於四時五行之布人君建維皇之極而
所以達政教之廣者未始不賴於公孤司府
之承然而君之於臣也其心一其任專故每
盡夫使下之道而臣之於君也其分懸其事
蹟或未篤夫事上之誠於此而欲馭之有方
===
以致乎相孚之美賴之協助以臻夫至治之
隆必也仁義之相濟乎仁也者渥之以恩而
啓其報禮之重者也義也者裁之以法而格
其頗僻之私者也有恩以渥之則臣皆秉忠
愛之忱而不忍欺有法以裁之則臣皆存寅
畏之念而不敢欺愛畏之情交於中而靖恭
之節著於外由是百官盡克艱之道庶政有
維和之休猶之四時之各宣其氣也五行之
各司其候也而天道之運於上者自然高明
而悠久不言而成化矣此唐虞之世所以明

臣對：臣聞帝王之致治於無疆也，必君臣相孚而後成德業之盛，必仁義相濟而後得馭臣之方。何者？君猶天也，臣猶四時五行也。天道有默運之神，而所以普生成之功者，未始不由於四時五行之布；人君建維皇之極，而所以達政教之廣者，未始不賴於公孤司府之承。然而君之於臣也，其心一，其任專，故每盡夫使下之道；而臣之於君也，其分懸，其事蹟或未篤夫事上之誠。於此而欲馭之有方，以致乎相孚之美，賴之協助，以臻夫至治之隆，必也仁義之相濟乎！仁也者，渥之以恩而啓其報禮之重者也；義也者，裁之以法而格其頗僻之私者也。有恩以渥之，則臣皆秉忠愛之忱而不忍欺；有法以裁之，則臣皆存寅畏之念而不敢欺。愛畏之情交於中，而靖恭之節著於外。由是百官盡克艱之道，庶政有維和之休，猶之四時之各宣其氣也，五行之各司其候也。而天道之運於上者，自然高明而悠久，不言而成化矣。此唐虞之世所以明
translation_en:
Your servant Zhu Dashou 諸大綬.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, for emperors and kings to bring about good government without limit, ruler and ministers must trust one another before virtue and achievement can flourish; benevolence and righteousness must complement one another before the proper method of governing ministers can be attained. Why is this? The ruler is like Heaven; ministers are like the four seasons and the Five Phases. The Way of Heaven possesses the wondrous power of operating silently, yet its work of universally bringing things into being and nurturing them to completion has always depended upon the unfolding of the four seasons and the Five Phases. The ruler establishes the imperial ultimate standard, yet the extension of government and instruction far and wide has always depended upon the supporting service of the Three Dukes, the Three Solitary Dignitaries, and the officials of the various offices.

In his dealings with ministers, the ruler is single-minded and entrusts responsibilities wholeheartedly, and thus regularly fulfills the proper way of employing subordinates. Ministers, however, stand far below the ruler in rank, and their conduct may fall short of wholehearted sincerity in serving their superior [?]. In these circumstances, if one wishes to govern them properly, attain the excellence of mutual trust, and rely upon their assistance to reach the fullness of perfect government, surely benevolence and righteousness must complement one another! Benevolence means treating them generously with favor and awakening in them a profound sense of the duty to reciprocate such courtesy. Righteousness means regulating them through law and correcting their wayward selfishness. When favor is bestowed generously upon them, ministers all cherish sincere loyalty and affection and cannot bear to deceive. When law regulates them, ministers all maintain reverent apprehension and dare not deceive. Affection and awe mingle within, while a disposition of disciplined respect manifests itself outwardly.

Thus all officials fully pursue the way of shouldering difficult duties, and the many affairs of government enjoy the blessings of harmony. This is like each of the four seasons diffusing its own vital energy, and each of the Five Phases presiding over its appointed seasonal conditions. The Way of Heaven, operating above, is then naturally lofty and luminous, enduring without end, accomplishing transformation without speaking. translation_en:
…worthy ministers rejoiced and rose to action, and their Way accorded in a single purpose; virtue and achievement shone brilliantly, and their government attained an eminence enduring through the ages. Otherwise, if a ruler relied entirely on righteousness without treating his ministers generously with favor, their feelings and intentions would remain unconnected: this would certainly not fulfill the meaning of sharing one heart and one virtue. If he relied entirely on benevolence without restraining them through law, recognition of merit and condemnation of faults [?] would not be manifest. How could this bring to fulfillment their loyalty in conscientiously discharging their duties and offering their service? Thus, mutual trust between ruler and ministers is the foundation of virtue and achievement; benevolence and righteousness complementing one another constitute the method of governing ministers. The means of equaling the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and achieving good government without limit lie precisely in this alone.
I respectfully reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed with a firm, discerning, pure disposition and possesses the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and rectitude. Reverent and composed, you embody the Way and commune above with the wondrous workings of Heaven. Extending sincerity and entrusting responsibilities to others, you have truly advanced toward government guided by the great principles. Fulfilling human relationships and perfecting institutions, you wield the authority to govern and instruct as sovereign and teacher. Establishing the highest standard and the mean, you elucidate the subtle and profound learning of emperors and kings. Your civilizing commands spread throughout the Four Seas; your influence and instruction reach the eight extremities. Your virtue is already exalted, and your achievements already vast. Yet, though a sage, you do not regard yourself as one. You have summoned us, your servants, to court [?] and graciously bestowed your discerning questions upon us, asking about matters we have witnessed ourselves and the means within our knowledge and abilities.

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
臣草茅愚陋不能仰承
德意然人臣之道事君之義臣講之素矣敢不
披瀝以對揚萬一耶臣聞之傳曰天生民而
立之君蓋言天為萬物之祖而不能盡左右
之方故擇天聰明之盡者而隆之以君師之
任是代天之道者君也當以天之心為心者
也禮曰設官分職以為民極蓋言君出庶物
之首而不能兼百職之繁故擇賢才之可任
者而委之以輔理之責是代君之事者臣也
當以君之心為心者也君以天之心為心其
===
道法天而不私以無心成化為至故君道常
主乎逸臣以君之心為心其道從君而不貳
以夙夜匪懈為至故臣道常主乎勞粤稽諸
古帝堯之德欽明文思允恭克讓固至極而
無以加矣然其所以致時雍於變之休者堯
非獨為之勞也當時若羲和授時舜納百揆
益烈山澤禹抑洪水孰非賢良之臣為之疇
咨若采而分理協助於下耶故稱堯之治者
謂之則天言其同天之無為而蕩蕩乎無能
名也帝舜之德濬哲文明温恭允塞亦至極

translation_en:
Your servant, an ignorant and uncultivated man from the countryside, cannot adequately receive Your Majesty’s gracious intentions. Yet I have long studied the way of a minister and the obligations of serving a sovereign. How could I dare not lay bare my heart in reply, to acknowledge even a ten-thousandth part of your grace? Your servant has heard it said in the Commentary: “Heaven brought forth the people and established a ruler over them.” This means that Heaven is the progenitor of all things, yet cannot exhaust every means of assisting them. It therefore chooses one who possesses heavenly intelligence to the fullest [?] and exalts him with the charge of ruler and teacher. Thus it is the ruler who carries out Heaven’s Way on its behalf, and he must take Heaven’s heart as his own. The Book of Rites says: “Establish offices and divide duties, thereby providing a standard for the people.” This means that the ruler stands at the head of all things, yet cannot personally undertake the manifold duties of all offices. He therefore selects worthy and talented men fit for appointment and entrusts them with the responsibility of assisting in government. Thus it is ministers who conduct the ruler’s affairs on his behalf, and they must take the ruler’s heart as their own. When the ruler takes Heaven’s heart as his own, his way is to emulate Heaven without partiality, attaining perfection by bringing about transformation without deliberate intent. Hence the ruler’s way chiefly rests in ease. When ministers take the ruler’s heart as their own, their way is to follow the ruler without divided loyalty, attaining perfection by remaining untiring morning and night. Hence the minister’s way chiefly rests in toil.
Let us examine antiquity. Emperor Yao’s virtues—reverence, intelligence, refinement, thoughtfulness, true respectfulness, and an ability to yield—had indeed reached perfection and could admit no addition. Yet the blessed transformation of the people into harmony was not achieved through Yao’s toil alone. In his day, Xi and He determined the seasons; Shun assumed charge of the hundred affairs; Yi burned the vegetation of mountains and marshes; and Yu checked the floodwaters. Were these not all worthy ministers whom he consulted and whose advice he followed, and who apportioned the work of government and assisted him from below? Thus those who praised Yao’s government said that he took Heaven as his model: they meant that, like Heaven, he acted without contrivance, and his greatness was so vast that none could find words to name it. Emperor Shun’s virtues—profound wisdom, cultured enlightenment, warmth, respectfulness, and true sincerity—likewise reached perfection…
