…and could be enhanced no further. Yet the ordered rule through which his influence stirred all four quarters was not achieved by Shun’s labors alone. In his time, Gao Yao clarified the punishments, Ji taught sowing and reaping, Bo Yi oversaw ritual, and Hou Kui made music. Were these not all worthy and capable ministers who exerted their abilities and advanced his undertakings, sharing the work of government and assisting him from below? Thus those who praised Shun’s rule called it government through nonaction: having secured the right men, he enjoyed great ease, and his abundant virtue was praised as unsurpassable. In speaking of government, the ages of Tang and Yu may indeed be called the pinnacle; in speaking of rulers, Yao and Shun may be considered beyond criticism. Yet even they necessarily relied on their ministers and close advisers in this way. That the ruler should enjoy ease while his ministers undertake the labor is therefore the constant order of Heaven and Earth and the settled judgment of all ages. But whereas the ruler regards all under Heaven as a single body, ministers sometimes concern themselves selfishly with their own persons; whereas the ruler regards all under Heaven as a single household, ministers sometimes seek only their own families’ advantage. From the Han and Tang down to the Song and Yuan, the temper of the times grew daily more superficial, and simple, substantial virtues gradually dissipated. Although there were loyal ministers and worthy chief councilors deserving praise, instances in which all officials learned from one another, as in the flourishing ancient ages of Tang and Yu, were surely seldom to be found.
We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao responded to Heaven’s appointed time and founded the dynasty, uniting all under Heaven and establishing the supreme standard. 一體者矣三公九卿百司庶府罔覆幬之化
而共荷夫生成浹雨露之恩而咸思夫報稱
固亦相淬勵勉自修省以求不忝於厥職
無媿於乃心然而人心不同智愚相越即今
觀之臣未敢謂盡如唐虞諸臣之良也亦未
敢謂盡如
國初諸臣之盛也臣伏讀
□制有曰夫以古之元首股肱眞是一體上下相
punctuated: 太祖天錫神聖，而馭臣有方，實亦一時諸臣慶知遇之隆，秉匪躬之節，忠愛而不忍欺，寅畏而不敢欺也。今我皇上久道成化，純心用賢，委任之專也，讒間不能携其情；責成之久也，進退得以行其志。一有微能，則因能而授之任，不惜夫爵秩之隆；一有微功，則因功而加之賞，不靳夫匪頒之賜。至於禮意之優渥，盎乎若陽春；訓諭之叮嚀，藹然如父子。陛下之所以待羣臣者，真可謂推心置腹而相待一體者矣。三公九卿、百司庶府，囿覆幬之化而共荷夫生成，浹雨露之恩而咸思夫報稱，固亦更相淬勵，勉自修省，以求不忝於厥職，無媿於乃心。然而人心不同，智愚相越，即今觀之，臣未敢謂盡如唐虞諸臣之良也，亦未敢謂盡如國初諸臣之盛也。臣伏讀上制，有曰：「夫以古之元首股肱，真是一體，上下相
translation_en:
…Taizu was endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom and governed his ministers by proper methods; yet it was also because the ministers of that time rejoiced in the extraordinary recognition and favor they received and upheld their selfless devotion to duty. In their loyalty and affection they could not bear to deceive him; in their reverence and awe they dared not deceive him.

Now our Emperor, through enduring adherence to the Way, has brought about transforming rule and employs worthy men with wholehearted sincerity. So complete is his trust in those entrusted with office that slander and attempts to sow discord cannot estrange their affections; so sustained is his expectation of accomplishment that, in advancing or withdrawing, they can carry out their aspirations. Whenever someone possesses even a modest ability, he assigns him responsibilities suited to that ability, unstinting in the exalted titles and ranks he bestows. Whenever someone renders even a modest service, he rewards him according to that service, withholding none of his lavish gifts. His generous courtesy is as abundant as the warmth of spring; his earnest instructions are as affectionate as those between father and son. Your Majesty’s treatment of your ministers may truly be called opening your heart to them and treating them as members of one body.

The Three Dukes and Nine Ministers, together with the officials of all offices and bureaus, dwell within the transforming influence that shelters them and share in its life-giving nurture. Steeped in favor like rain and dew, all think of making a fitting return. They do indeed encourage and spur one another onward, striving to cultivate and examine themselves, seeking neither to disgrace their offices nor to feel shame in their hearts. Yet human hearts differ, and the wise and foolish are far apart. Looking at the present, your servant dares not say that all equal the excellence of the ministers of Tang and Yu, nor dares he say that all equal the distinction of the ministers at the founding of our dynasty.

Your servant has reverently read the imperial decree, which says: “In antiquity, the sovereign as head and the ministers as limbs truly formed one body, with those above and below mutually…”

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
資不若茲時之大不同者朕以心腹置人心腹
中何乃視我仇讎焉安望為國恤民也臣因是
仰窺
陛下之心任賢所以為國使臣將以恤民是誠以
天之心為心者也凡茲臣庶咸宜以
陛下之心為心而今有不盡然者將安所逃於天
地間耶然臣嘗聞之治世非無小人自難乎
其為小人亂世非無君子自難乎其為君子
方
今道協太和世登盛治而諸臣之中間有不率
===
者是亦治世之小人也不可以是槩視諸臣
也顧所以馭之何如耳今夫元首股肱相為
一體君上臣下道每相資非古之時為然而
今獨不然也良以古之人心即今之人心而
今之士習非古之士習古之人臣其視君真
猶元首也其事是君真猶股肱之衛元首也
皆根於心之不可解而發於情之不可遏愛
而彌篤不敢有一毫之自私也敬而罔怠不
敢有一毫之自肆也而今之事君則有不盡
然者坐而論道非無秉忠竭誠之臣而懷欺

…supported one another, unlike the great discord of the present time. I place my own heart within the hearts of others; why, then, do they regard me as an enemy? How can I expect them to serve the state and care for the people?” From this, your servant reverently discerns Your Majesty’s intention: you appoint worthy men to serve the state and employ ministers to care for the people. This truly is to take Heaven’s heart as your own. All these ministers and subjects ought to take Your Majesty’s heart as their own. Yet some today do not fully do so: where between Heaven and Earth could they escape? Your servant has heard, however, that an age of good government is not without petty men, but makes it difficult for them to act as petty men; an age of disorder is not without gentlemen, but makes it difficult for them to act as gentlemen. Now the Way accords with supreme harmony, and the age has attained flourishing government. Those among the ministers who occasionally fail to comply are simply the petty men of a well-governed age. One must not judge all ministers by them; the question is simply how they are governed.

The head and the limbs together form one body; the ruler above and the ministers below constantly sustain one another in the Way. It is not that this was so in antiquity and is uniquely otherwise today. Indeed, the human heart of antiquity is the human heart of today, but the habits of today’s scholars are not those of antiquity. Ministers of antiquity truly regarded their ruler as the head; in serving him, they were truly like limbs protecting the head. All this was rooted in an attachment of the heart that could not be severed and issued from feelings that could not be restrained. Their love grew ever more devoted, and they dared not harbor the slightest selfishness; their reverence never slackened, and they dared not indulge themselves in the slightest. Among those who serve rulers today, however, some do not fully act in this way. Among those who sit and discuss the Way, there are certainly ministers who uphold loyalty and exert their utmost sincerity; yet those who harbor deceit…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
狗黨者亦容有之矣起而作事非無效忠宣
力之臣而怠事苟祿者亦容有之矣藩屏四
方固有旬宣而惠和者而尸素養望亦未必
其盡無也擁麾分閫固有戮力而矢心者而
損威失重亦未必其盡無也此其心非始於
一念之自私則始於一念之自肆惟自私則
忠愛之心疎而不能懇切真誠以服勤乎王
事惟自肆則敬畏之心怠而不能嚴恭儼恪
以祇若乎明威以此為國安望其輔理之功
以此為民安望其勤恤之政此誠有如
===
陛下之所諭也然而自負其心則亦自貽其戚若
萬物之自棄於大造而奚虧於天地之化乎
若人子之自乖夫順德而奚損於父母之慈
乎
聖制乃曰朕固無知人之哲能官之智而下詢臣
等以知能之方臣竊仰見
陛下離照無私明見萬里之外
乾剛獨斷總裁庶政之幾別邪正之途而凡臣
庶之隱幽咸得其情一日月之照臨而萬物
莫不被其光也盡器使之道而凡大臣之任

…there may also be those who collude in factions [?]. Among those who undertake affairs, there are certainly ministers who demonstrate loyalty and exert their strength, yet there may also be those who neglect their duties and merely draw their stipends. Among those who serve as bulwarks throughout the realm, there are certainly men who disseminate imperial governance and bring benevolence and harmony; yet it cannot be said that none hold office idly, enjoying its emoluments while cultivating their reputations. Among those who bear command banners and exercise regional military authority, there are certainly men who devote their strength and pledge their hearts; yet it cannot be said that none diminish their authority and lose their standing. Such dispositions begin either with a single selfish thought or with a single self-indulgent thought. Selfishness weakens their loyalty and love, preventing them from serving diligently in royal affairs with earnest sincerity. Self-indulgence slackens their reverence and awe, preventing them from obeying Your Majesty’s manifest authority with solemn respect. If they serve the state in this manner, how can one expect them to assist its governance? If they serve the people in this manner, how can one expect diligent and compassionate administration? This is indeed as Your Majesty has instructed. Yet, by betraying their own hearts, they bring distress upon themselves. It is as though the myriad things cast themselves out of the great process of creation: how could this impair the transforming work of Heaven and Earth? It is as though a child departed from the virtue of obedience: how could this diminish parental love?
Yet the Emperor’s decree reads: “I assuredly lack the discernment to understand men and the wisdom to appoint capable officials.” Your Majesty then condescended to ask us, your servants, about the means of discerning men and appointing the capable. Your servant respectfully perceives that Your Majesty’s illumination, like that of the trigram Li, is impartial and sees clearly beyond ten thousand li. With the strength of the trigram Qian, you decide independently and direct the critical workings of all affairs of government. You distinguish the paths of wickedness and uprightness and fully apprehend the hidden circumstances of officials and commoners alike. Like the sun and moon shining upon the world, your light reaches every being. You fully realize the principle of employing men according to their capacities, and as for the appointment of the great ministers…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
使各因其才一四時之順布而萬物莫不得
其所也然則知人之哲能官之智固已曠千
古而同符堯舜矣臣愚一得之見則有仁義
相須之說焉謂之仁者非姑息之謂也念一
體之係而推容保之恩使之親而不相間耳
謂之義者非刻薄之謂也防慈愛之流而用
威克之道使之尊而不相玩耳斯二者在
陛下已預養而時出之而臣復以此為言者盖以
諸臣之中賢否殊途固有戴仁以圖報者矣
而亦有見義而後懲固有感恩以作忠者矣
===
而亦有畏法而後勸殆不可以一律齊也今
陛下之於臣寵之以祿秩榮之以聲名忠信以孚
其心禮儀以重其任仁無不至矣意者一於
慈惠則惠褻而不以為恩過於寵榮則寵加
而不以為德秉忠竭誠者任之彌專可也其
或懷欺而狥黨則天討之彰可不行歟效忠
宣力者委之不貳可也其或怠事而苟祿則
廢黜之典可不舉歟旬宣惠和者進之崇階
可也其或尸素而養望則三載之考可不嚴
歟戮力矢心者託之閫外可也其或損威而

Thus Your Majesty’s discernment in judging men and wisdom in appointing officials have surely surpassed the ages and accord with those of Yao and Shun. I mean remembering the bond that unites ruler and ministers as one body and extending the grace of tolerance and protection, so that they remain close, without estrangement. By righteousness I do not mean harshness. I mean guarding against the excesses of affectionate kindness and employing the discipline of authority, so that they remain respectful, without presumption. Your Majesty has already cultivated both these qualities and manifests them as occasion requires. Yet I speak of them again because, among your ministers, the worthy and the unworthy follow different paths. There are certainly those who cherish your benevolence and seek to repay it, but there are also those who amend their conduct only after encountering righteousness. Yet perhaps, if kindness and generosity alone prevail, your favors will become commonplace and cease to be regarded as grace; if favor and honor are excessive, further favor will cease to be regarded as beneficence. Those who uphold loyalty and devote themselves wholeheartedly may properly be entrusted with still greater responsibility. Those who render loyal service and exert their strength may properly be entrusted with duties without misgivings. title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
失重則三錫之命可不慎歟又或間行不測
之威以懾奸宄之志時申核實之令以稽文
飾之奸某稱賢能也必審其賢能之實而名
浮於德者在所不庸某稱課最也必核其課
最之詳而祿浮於功者在所必黜某也任某
事克勝其任旌之可也苟受直而怠事則懲
其瘝曠之愆某也舉某人不負所舉賞之可
也苟阿好而徇私則治其欺罔之罪推而至
於天下之大四海之廣由大臣以督監司由
監司以督守令潢池之弄兵未息則知其保
===
障之才疎閭閻之貧困未蘇則知其催科之
政急嚴明乎賞罰而大起精明之功振肅乎
紀綱而痛革因循之弊使天下洗滌心志聚

明斷相資而坐而論道者罔不良矣為汲黯
之鎮重社稷為陸贄之竭忠賛襄而起而作
事者罔不勤矣在外者效承宣之能而思所
以供其職為龔遂之寢冦渤海為文翁之興
學成都而藩屏四方者罔不循矣為裴度之
削平淮蔡為韓琦之坐懾西羌而擁麾分閫
者罔不競矣元首明於上而股肱懐勵翼之
誠腹心置於人而手足效維持之義如此而
喜起賡歌之盛豈徒專美於唐虞而已哉此
非臣之私言也唐虞之時都俞吁咈而上下

其道固所以相濟而不可以相無也然臣又

之道和風甘雨長養萬物其機未嘗或息而

…complementing one another through clear judgment, so that all who sit in council to discuss the Way will be worthy. They will emulate Ji An in safeguarding the altars of soil and grain through his steadfast presence, and Lu Zhi in giving his utmost loyalty in assistance, so that all who rise to undertake affairs will be diligent. Those serving outside the capital will demonstrate their ability to receive and promulgate imperial commands and consider how to fulfill their duties. They will emulate Gong Sui in quelling banditry in Bohai and Wen Weng in promoting learning in Chengdu, so that all who serve as protective bulwarks throughout the realm will govern conscientiously. They will emulate Pei Du in pacifying Huai and Cai and Han Qi in overawing the western Qiang by his very presence, so that all who wield command banners and exercise regional military authority will exert themselves fully. The head will be enlightened above, while the arms and legs cherish sincere resolve to assist him diligently. He will entrust others with his innermost confidence, while his hands and feet fulfill their duty to sustain him. With things thus ordered, could the flourishing exchange of songs celebrating joyful service remain the exclusive glory of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun?

These are not merely your servant’s personal assertions. In the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, candid expressions of assent and dissent passed between ruler and ministers, and mutual trust prevailed between those above and below: we can readily imagine that atmosphere of supreme harmony. Yet in punishing the Four Evildoers, there was not the slightest indulgence. Thus, they never failed to temper their actions with righteousness. In the time of our Taizu, the assembled ministers united their hearts to accomplish the great undertaking together; the harmony of their feelings and intentions could indeed be called consummate. Yet distinctions were drawn between the worthy and the treacherous, and biographies were accordingly composed. Was this not likewise an exercise of judgment through righteousness?

Benevolence is the harmonious vital force of Heaven and Earth; righteousness is their stern vital force. The ruler succeeds Heaven in bringing forth good government and takes Heaven as his model in establishing the supreme standard. He therefore models himself on its harmony to practice benevolence and on its sternness to practice righteousness. These ways complement one another, and neither can dispense with the other. title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
雷霆之震霜雪之撃則時一見焉是仁義之
用雖天地固已酌而施之矣
陛下深仁厚澤淪浹人心如和風之鼓舞甘雨之
滋潤天下莫不被之而間一行義以遏惡懲
奸固有斷不至於過者然而體天之心憲天
之道寧過於仁而無過於義此實臣之所以
惓惓仰望於
陛下者也如事可罪也或原其過誤之情言雖戇
也或諒其忠誠之悃擴包荒之度而罪疑從
輕開遷善之門而刑過無小則天下皆知
===
陛下之用義也用乎其所當用者也其裁之以法
也裁乎其所不得不裁者也而凡人臣之沐
浴於深仁者固已德一而心同其自罹於罪
愆者亦皆心悅而誠服如萬物之於天地然
雖覆之而無憾如人子之於父母然雖勞之
而不怨矣此之謂仁育義正相兼相濟固不
以恩而廢法亦不以法而傷恩斯天地之全
德而帝王之中道也乃若張鼓舞之大機用
磨礪之大柄使天下士即未仕之初而預養
夫忠貞之志當既仕之日而益堅夫篤棐之

punctuated:
雷霆之震、霜雪之撃，則時一見焉。是仁義之用，雖天地，固已酌而施之矣。
陛下深仁厚澤，淪浹人心，如和風之鼓舞、甘雨之滋潤，天下莫不被之。而間一行義，以遏惡懲奸，固有斷不至於過者。然而體天之心，憲天之道，寧過於仁，而無過於義，此實臣之所以惓惓仰望於陛下者也。如事可罪也，或原其過誤之情；言雖戇也，或諒其忠誠之悃。擴包荒之度，而罪疑從輕；開遷善之門，而刑過無小。則天下皆知陛下之用義也，用乎其所當用者也；其裁之以法也，裁乎其所不得不裁者也。而凡人臣之沐浴於深仁者，固已德一而心同；其自罹於罪愆者，亦皆心悅而誠服。如萬物之於天地然，雖覆之而無憾；如人子之於父母然，雖勞之而不怨矣。此之謂仁育義正，相兼相濟，固不以恩而廢法，亦不以法而傷恩。斯天地之全德，而帝王之中道也。
乃若張鼓舞之大機，用磨礪之大柄，使天下士即未仕之初，而預養夫忠貞之志；當既仕之日，而益堅夫篤棐之
translation_en:
…whereas the crashing of thunder and the assaults of frost and snow appear only occasionally. Thus, even Heaven and Earth exercise benevolence and righteousness with due measure.
Your Majesty’s profound benevolence and abundant bounty penetrate the people’s hearts. Like the stirring of gentle winds and the nourishment of timely rain, they reach everyone under Heaven. When you occasionally exercise righteousness to restrain evil and punish the wicked, your decisions assuredly do not go to excess. Yet to embody Heaven’s heart and take Heaven’s Way as your model, you should sooner err on the side of benevolence than exceed due measure in righteousness. This is what your servant earnestly hopes for from Your Majesty. When a deed merits punishment, you might consider the circumstances of the error; although someone’s words are blunt, you might recognize the sincerity of his loyal intentions. Enlarge your capacity to tolerate shortcomings, giving the lighter penalty where guilt is doubtful; open the door to reform, while punishing transgressions however small [?]. Then all under Heaven will know that Your Majesty exercises righteousness where it ought to be exercised, and judges by law only where judgment cannot be avoided. All your subjects who bask in your profound benevolence will already be united in virtue and purpose; even those who bring guilt upon themselves will submit sincerely and willingly. They will be like the myriad creatures in their relation to Heaven and Earth, bearing no resentment even when destroyed, or like children in their relation to their parents, feeling no grievance even when made to toil. This is what is meant by nurturing through benevolence and correcting through righteousness, the two working together and supporting each other. Favor does not displace the law, nor does the law impair favor. This is the complete virtue of Heaven and Earth and the balanced Way of emperors and kings.
As for setting in motion the great mechanism of encouragement and wielding the great instrument of discipline, so that the scholars of the realm nurture aspirations to loyalty and constancy even before entering office, and, once in office, further strengthen their devoted support…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
貞則學校之教考課之法殆亦不可緩焉盖
學校之設風俗之關也今士初習句讀而其
心多以榮身肥家為圖則及其筮仕也授以
官秩而籍為媒利之階委以任使而視為肆
志之地為德為民養之無素而安望其能盡
然耶是故必重學校如古三物之教六德之
修使窮居之日已真知夫君臣之義如范仲
淹自秀才時遂以天下為己任則行義之際
庶幾不變其塞而忠君愛國自有所不容已
矣考課之典賢否之別也今庶官因緣為奸
===
而典銓或未得其情偽之實則雖亦猶夫考
課也然賢者未必褒而為善之心日弛不肖
者未必斥而僥倖之心日甚黜陟幽明不無
失當而安望其能勸懲耶是故必嚴考課如
古八法之治六條之察使不才之流不得濫
夫名器之重如三代盛時官不及私昵爵罔
及惡德則忠良之臣庶幾益加激勸而鞠躬
盡瘁亦在所不敢辭矣此二者亦皆所以行
仁義之道而感率人臣以效忠者也若夫明
哲以知人論官而器使則固

…steadfastness, then instruction in schools and the system of evaluating officials surely must not be neglected either. The establishment of schools is pivotal to prevailing customs. Nowadays, when scholars first learn to parse sentences, their minds are often already bent on winning personal glory and enriching their families. Thus, when they enter official service, they treat the rank conferred upon them as a stepping-stone to profit, and the duties entrusted to them as an arena for indulging their desires. Having never been nurtured in virtue and service to the people, how can they be expected to fulfill these responsibilities? Schools must therefore be given due importance, following the ancient instruction in the three categories and cultivation of the six virtues, so that even while living in obscurity scholars already truly understand the obligations between ruler and minister. Fan Zhongyan, from his days as a student, took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. Following his example, when they put righteousness into practice, they may remain unchanged in their integrity [?], and their loyalty to the ruler and love for the realm will be impulses they cannot suppress.
The institution of official evaluation distinguishes the worthy from the unworthy. Nowadays, officials exploit connections to commit wrongdoing, while those responsible for selection may fail to ascertain their true character or deceit. Although evaluations are still conducted, the worthy are not necessarily commended, and their resolve to do good weakens daily; the unworthy are not necessarily dismissed, and their hopes of gaining through luck grow daily. Demotions and promotions of the undeserving and deserving are not free from error: how, then, can evaluations be expected to encourage good conduct and deter misconduct? Official evaluation must therefore be made rigorous, following the ancient administration by the eight regulations and scrutiny under the six articles, so that incompetent men cannot improperly occupy weighty offices and ranks. As in the flourishing days of the Three Dynasties, offices should not go to personal favorites, nor titles to men of evil character. 陛下德明德威之餘事耳，而臣又何容贅耶？抑臣又有獻焉：仁義之德，原於天而根於心。心焉既正，則一念之慈愛即為仁，一念之裁制即為義。時而出之，並行而不悖；舉而措之，參和而不偏，皆此心之妙用焉耳。
臣願陛下益純敬一之功，懋養淵源之德，澄心正極，省慮涵虛。有敬止之純矣，而務底於緝熈；有剛健之體矣，而必期於不息。則精明之中，萬理咸備；公溥之內，至德渾全。存諸中，可以合天心；達諸外，可以發天機。時焉以仁而用恩，即天之和煦而不流也；時焉以法而用義，即天之肅烈而不過也。王道普和平之美，庶官成效順之風，至治保於無疆，而萬壽引於弗替。天下幸甚，臣愚幸甚！臣不識忌諱，冒瀆宸嚴，無任戰兢隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
…are merely incidental accomplishments of Your Majesty’s illuminating virtue and awe-inspiring virtue. What further words could your servant possibly add? Yet your servant has another offering to make. The virtues of benevolence and righteousness originate in Heaven and take root in the heart. Once the heart is upright, a single thought of loving kindness constitutes benevolence, and a single thought of judgment and restraint constitutes righteousness. Expressed at the proper times, they operate together without conflict; put into practice, they blend harmoniously without partiality. All are simply the wondrous workings of this heart.
Your servant wishes that Your Majesty may further perfect your cultivation of reverent single-mindedness, diligently nourish virtue at its source, clear your heart and establish the proper standard, and lessen distracting thoughts while nurturing inner receptivity. Already possessing the purity of abiding in reverence, strive to attain ever-continuing brightness; already possessing the substance of strength and vigor, resolve that it shall never cease. Then, within your lucid understanding, all principles will be present; within your impartiality and breadth, consummate virtue will be whole and complete. Preserved within, it can accord with Heaven’s heart; expressed outwardly, it can bring forth Heaven’s workings. When, as circumstances require, you exercise benevolence and bestow favor, this will be Heaven’s gentle warmth, without indulgence. When, as circumstances require, you apply the law and exercise righteousness, this will be Heaven’s stern severity, without excess. The Kingly Way will spread the blessings of peace and harmony everywhere, and all officials will establish a spirit of obedient service. Perfect governance will be preserved without limit, and your myriad years of longevity will continue without decline. How fortunate for all under Heaven! How fortunate for your foolish servant! Your servant, ignorant of what must not be spoken, has presumptuously offended your august majesty. I cannot contain my utmost trembling and dread of ruin. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
臣陶大臨
臣對臣聞帝王之致治也有兼照之智而後
可以彰天下之大化有總攬之權而後可以
執天下之大機何謂兼照之智核功能之實
察淑慝之情精明而不爽者是也何謂總攬
之權嚴黜陟之典昭激勸之公鼓舞而不倦
者是也智以燭其微則忠邪誠偽之辨得於
神明洞達之中猶萬物之照臨於日月而幽
顯不得以遁其形權以妙其用則進退予奪
之宜得於震勵作新之下猶萬物之鼓動於
===
風霆而大小咸得以著其性是故辨官以智
聖人之明也惟明則知人之哲以得而所以
振作者有其基矣馭臣以權聖人之公也惟
公則官人之能以盡而所以鑒別者致其實
矣此仁智合一之道剛明並運之理帝王所
以開昭融之化以隆上下之交寓作新之機
以弘德業之會者也明良喜起之風雍煕太
和之治豈復有外於此哉欽惟
皇帝陛下秉
天縱之資撫日中之美繼

translation_en:
Your servant, Tao Dalin.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, in bringing about good government, emperors and kings must possess wisdom that illuminates all things before they can manifest the great transforming influence throughout the realm; they must possess authority that commands the whole before they can grasp the great mainspring of the realm. What is wisdom that illuminates all things? It means verifying actual achievements and abilities, discerning the true circumstances of goodness and wickedness, and being perceptive without error. What is authority that commands the whole? It means rigorously enforcing the rules for dismissal and promotion, making manifest the impartiality of incentives and encouragement, and inspiring others without weariness. When wisdom illuminates the subtlest things, distinctions between loyalty and treachery, sincerity and deceit emerge through inspired insight and penetrating understanding. This is like the sun and moon shining upon the myriad things: whether hidden or manifest, none can conceal its form. When authority is exercised with consummate skill, appropriate decisions about advancement and dismissal, granting and withholding emerge through rousing, exhorting, and renewing. This is like wind and thunder stirring the myriad things: great and small alike can manifest their natures.

Thus, to distinguish among officials through wisdom is the sage’s perspicacity. Only through perspicacity can one attain the discernment needed to know men, thereby establishing a foundation for rousing them to action. To govern ministers through authority is the sage’s impartiality. Only through impartiality can one fully exercise the ability to appoint men to office, thereby giving practical substance to discernment. This is the Way in which benevolence and wisdom unite, the principle by which firmness and perspicacity operate together. Through it, emperors and kings inaugurate a luminous and harmonious transforming influence, strengthening relations between superiors and subordinates; they embody the impetus for renewal, bringing virtue and achievement together on a grand scale. Could the spirit in which an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers joyfully rouse one another, or the governance of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony, lie anywhere outside this?

乾剛以用權鼓舞神於莫測本之以敬
天勤民之心措之為知人安民之政蓋自古帝王
所罕及者矣迺者因委任失稱遂有感於知
人之哲能官之智而

…the radiance of Li to illuminate all things, with discernment residing in you before the first stirrings of events; you rouse the firmness of Qian to exercise authority, inspiring and encouraging others with an unfathomable efficacy. You ground this in a heart that reveres Heaven and labors for the people, and put it into practice through government that recognizes worthy men and brings peace to the people. Such achievements have rarely been equaled by emperors and kings since antiquity. Recently, because appointments failed to match the responsibilities entrusted, you were moved to consider the sagacity of recognizing men and the wisdom of assigning them suitable offices, and your enlightened questions have addressed these matters. Your servant, dwelling obscurely among the common people, has received from afar the transforming influence of your rule and has long cherished a loyal heart. Moreover, having personally encountered this age of enlightened sageliness, witnessed your means of exhortation and encouragement, and been privileged to receive your words and offer myself in service, how could I dare not lay bare my humble sincerity and respectfully address the matters about which Your Majesty has asked?
Your servant has heard that the relationship between ruler and minister involves both the duties of their respective stations and bonds of affection. The Book of Changes associates the ruler’s way with Qian and the minister’s way with Kun: this expresses the distinction between their stations. The Book of Documents calls the ruler the head and the ministers the legs and arms: this expresses their bonds of affection. Since the distinctions of station must be strictly maintained, a minister must look up to his ruler as to Heaven and dare not evade his duty of obedience and service. This is how he fully discharges the obligations of his station. Anyone harboring even a single thought lacking reverence is not a minister of unalloyed loyalty. Since the bonds of affection must not slacken, a minister must honor his ruler as the head and be unable to restrain his sincere devotion to defending him. This is how he fully expresses that affection. Anyone harboring even a single thought lacking wholehearted devotion is not a minister of unalloyed loyalty. These principles originate in Heaven’s mandate and are inherent in the human heart. They are truly the standard for ministers in every age, to be fulfilled without waiting for the ruler’s supervision and reproaches. Yet human hearts differ, and even in a flourishing…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
世不能無小人此精明之智鼓舞之權尤帝
王制馭臣鄰之要而不可或忽也臣伏讀
聖制有曰朕惟天命立君以宰於率土必有分理
協助之臣所謂鄰哉也吁堯舜之克聖不有高
賢大良之助豈二聖獨勞耶是道也天之道也
堯舜以來未之有改也今夫天運於上未嘗
有所勞也然序之以四時之吏使各司其令
不相僭忒焉則錯行成歲者莫非上天之功
布之以五行之佐使各宣其氣不相凌混焉
則分職成形者莫非上天之德堯舜法天立

以求盡理天下之事哉奚考其時以平水土

山澤則有益以作納言則有龍以撰時治曆
則有羲和以典禮典樂則有夷夔內有九官
而總之百揆所以分治於內也外設十二牧
而總之四岳所以分治於外也盖堯舜以諸
punctuated:
世不能無小人，此精明之智、鼓舞之權，尤帝王制馭臣鄰之要，而不可或忽也。臣伏讀聖制，有曰：「朕惟天命立君，以宰於率土，必有分理協助之臣，所謂鄰哉也。吁！堯舜之克聖，不有高賢大良之助，豈二聖獨勞耶？」是道也，天之道也，堯舜以來未之有改也。
今夫天運於上，未嘗有所勞也。然序之以四時之吏，使各司其令，不相僭忒焉，則錯行成歲者，莫非上天之功；布之以五行之佐，使各宣其氣，不相凌混焉，則分職成形者，莫非上天之德。堯舜，法天立極者也。語其德，則精一執中，天下之稱盛德者所必歸也；語其化，則時雍風動，天下之稱大業者所必歸也。然豈紛紛焉自竭其智能，以求盡理天下之事哉？奚考其時，以平水土則有禹，以教稼穡則有稷，以敷五教則有契，以明五刑則有皐陶，以若予工則有垂，以掌山澤則有益，以作納言則有龍，以授時治曆則有羲和，以典禮典樂則有夷夔。內有九官，而總之百揆，所以分治於內也；外設十二牧，而總之四岳，所以分治於外也。蓋堯舜以諸
translation_en:
…even an age of flourishing rule cannot be without petty men. Thus penetrating discernment and the authority to inspire and motivate are especially essential to an emperor’s direction and control of his ministers, and must never be neglected. Your servant has reverently read Your Majesty’s decree, which says: “I consider that Heaven’s mandate establishes a ruler to govern all the land; he must have ministers who share the work of administration and assist him—those described as his ‘neighbors.’ Ah! Could Yao and Shun have attained sagehood without the assistance of lofty worthies and outstanding men of ability? Could those two sages have labored alone?” This way is Heaven’s way; since Yao and Shun it has never changed.
Now Heaven moves above without ever exerting itself. Yet it orders its operations through the officers of the four seasons, each carrying out the ordinances proper to his season without encroachment or error. Their alternating courses complete the year, and all this is the achievement of Heaven above. It distributes its operations through the assistants of the Five Phases, each giving expression to its own vital force without mutual interference or confusion. Their separate functions bring things into form, and all this is the virtue of Heaven above. Yao and Shun modeled themselves on Heaven and established the highest standard. As for their virtue, they were discerning and single-minded, holding fast to the mean: all under Heaven who speak of consummate virtue must turn to them. As for their transforming influence, it brought harmony and moved people as the wind moves things: all under Heaven who speak of great achievements must turn to them. Yet did they busily exhaust their own intelligence and abilities in an effort to manage every affair under Heaven?
Examining their time [?], we find Yu to regulate the waters and land; Ji to teach sowing and reaping; Xie to disseminate the five teachings; Gao Yao to clarify the five punishments; Chui to oversee ‘my craftsmen’; Yi to administer the mountains and marshes; Long to serve as Chief of Communications; Xi and He to announce the seasons and regulate the calendar; and Yi and Kui to direct ritual and music. Within the central government were nine officers, coordinated by the Chief Minister, thereby dividing responsibility for administration at the center. Outside it were twelve Regional Governors, coordinated by the Four Chiefs, thereby dividing responsibility for administration in the regions. Thus Yao and Shun took the various…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
臣之能為能故中心無為而不見其為逸諸
臣以堯舜之心為心故左右厥辟而不言其
為勞凡所以亮天工熈帝載者交盡於二聖
之朝而相得於一堂之上志意浹洽精神流
貫若一人之身天君泰然黙運於中而肢體
形氣莫不以其能效用於外不待告戒命令
而其應自神誠有如
聖諭所謂元首股肱真是一體者降而三代禹湯
文武之為君伊傅周召之為臣其治浹化隆
固先後一揆而同心同德實授受一轍盖君
===
必得臣斯可以弘化理之責君之所資於臣
者固甚殷而臣必得君斯可以顯經濟之猷
臣之所資於君者亦甚切此天地之常經古
今之通義何今之人莫由斯道而致煩
陛下之慮耶臣又伏讀
聖制有曰朕以心腹置人心腹中何乃視我仇讐
焉安望為國恤民也臣愚於此盖已仰見
陛下厚下之仁而深有慨於當事者之或不盡其
誠矣夫
陛下尊禮大臣有隆勿替體念羣臣遐邇不遺

punctuated:
臣之能為能，故中心無為，而不見其為逸；諸臣以堯舜之心為心，故左右厥辟，而不言其為勞。凡所以亮天工、熈帝載者，交盡於二聖之朝，而相得於一堂之上。志意浹洽，精神流貫，若一人之身，天君泰然，黙運於中，而肢體形氣莫不以其能效用於外，不待告戒命令，而其應自神。誠有如聖諭所謂「元首股肱真是一體」者。降而三代，禹湯文武之為君，伊傅周召之為臣，其治浹化隆，固先後一揆，而同心同德，實授受一轍。盖君必得臣，斯可以弘化理之責，君之所資於臣者固甚殷；而臣必得君，斯可以顯經濟之猷，臣之所資於君者亦甚切。此天地之常經，古今之通義，何今之人莫由斯道，而致煩陛下之慮耶？
臣又伏讀聖制有曰：「朕以心腹置人心腹中，何乃視我仇讐焉？安望為國恤民也？」臣愚於此，盖已仰見陛下厚下之仁，而深有慨於當事者之或不盡其誠矣。夫陛下尊禮大臣，有隆勿替；體念羣臣，遐邇不遺。
translation_en:
…their ministers’ abilities as their own. Thus they remained inwardly free of action, yet were not seen as idle. Their ministers took the hearts of Yao and Shun as their own; thus they assisted their sovereigns without speaking of their service as toil. All that served to assist Heaven’s work and glorify the emperors’ undertakings was jointly fulfilled at the courts of these two sages, with ruler and ministers finding mutual accord within a single hall. Their purposes were in complete harmony, their vital spirits flowing through one another like those of a single body: the mind, its sovereign, rested serenely and operated silently within, while limbs, bodily form, and vital energies all exercised their abilities outwardly. Without awaiting admonitions or commands, their responses were wondrous of themselves. This truly accords with what Your Majesty’s sacred instruction calls “the head and the limbs truly forming a single body.” Coming down to the Three Dynasties, there were Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as rulers, and Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao as ministers. Their government was all-pervading and their transforming influence flourished. Earlier and later alike followed one standard; their unity of purpose and virtue likewise followed a single transmitted course. For a ruler must find worthy ministers before he can fully discharge his responsibility for moral transformation and good government: his reliance upon his ministers is indeed profound. A minister, in turn, must find a worthy ruler before he can give effect to his plans for ordering the realm: his reliance upon his ruler is likewise pressing. This is the enduring norm of Heaven and Earth and the principle common to antiquity and the present. Why do the men of today fail to follow this way, thereby troubling Your Majesty with concern?
Your servant has also reverently read these words in Your Majesty’s composition: “I place my own heart within the hearts of others. Why, then, do they regard me as an enemy? How can I expect them to serve the state and care for the people?” Though foolish, your servant can already discern herein Your Majesty’s benevolence in generously treating your subordinates, and feels deep distress that those entrusted with affairs may not devote their full sincerity to you. Your Majesty’s respectful and courteous treatment of the great ministers grows ever greater and never diminishes; your sympathetic concern for all your ministers leaves out none, whether near or far…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
恩意之優渥
敎戒之叮嚀開心腹見情素而一毫勉强疑忌
之意無所存於其間雖堯舜之待其臣未有
能過此者感恩而效忠乘時而思奮當必有
稷契諸臣以體
陛下欽崇天道之心以副
陛下惠安元元之意矣而人之度量知愚相越有
不可以一律齊者故方今之臣其在
朝廷輦轂固必有謨明弼諧之臣矣然而違上
所好負慢自賢者未盡無也其在百工庶府
===
固必有秉義竭忠之臣矣然而罔上行私朋
家作讎者未盡無也其在藩臬郡邑固必有
旬宣惠和之臣矣然而剥民自豐為國斂怨
者未盡無也其在捍衛守禦固必有死綏許
國之臣矣然而偷懦無為全身苟免者未盡
無也甚至私援引以市恩公賄賂以干憲外
有事君之名内無事君之實夫是以分理之
責或有所未供協助之職或有所未盡委任
隆遇之誠或有所孤負而不得以善乎其後
陛下之所以待臣者如此其厚而臣之所自處者

punctuated: 恩意之優渥，敎戒之叮嚀，開心腹，見情素，而一毫勉强疑忌之意無所存於其間，雖堯舜之待其臣，未有能過此者。感恩而效忠，乘時而思奮，當必有稷契諸臣，以體陛下欽崇天道之心，以副陛下惠安元元之意矣。而人之度量知愚相越，有不可以一律齊者。故方今之臣，其在朝廷輦轂，固必有謨明弼諧之臣矣；然而違上所好，負慢自賢者，未盡無也。其在百工庶府，固必有秉義竭忠之臣矣；然而罔上行私，朋家作讎者，未盡無也。其在藩臬郡邑，固必有旬宣惠和之臣矣；然而剥民自豐，為國斂怨者，未盡無也。其在捍衛守禦，固必有死綏許國之臣矣；然而偷懦無為，全身苟免者，未盡無也。甚至私援引以市恩，公賄賂以干憲，外有事君之名，内無事君之實。夫是以分理之責或有所未供，協助之職或有所未盡，委任隆遇之誠或有所孤負，而不得以善乎其後。陛下之所以待臣者如此其厚，而臣之所自處者
translation_en:
…Your favor is so abundant, your instruction and admonitions so earnest. You open your heart and reveal your true feelings, without the slightest trace of reluctance, suspicion, or mistrust. Even Yao and Shun could not have surpassed this in their treatment of their ministers. Moved by gratitude to serve loyally, and eager to exert themselves when the opportunity arises, there surely must be ministers like Ji and Xie who embody Your Majesty’s reverence for the Way of Heaven and fulfill Your Majesty’s wish to benefit and bring peace to the common people. Yet people differ in breadth of mind, wisdom, and folly, and cannot all be measured by a single standard.

Thus, among today’s ministers serving at court in the capital, there surely are those who offer enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance. Yet there are also some who oppose what their sovereign favors, act arrogantly and disrespectfully, and consider themselves superior. Among those serving in the various offices and government bureaus, there surely are ministers who uphold righteousness and devote themselves utterly to loyal service. Yet there are also some who deceive their sovereign, pursue private interests, and form factions among powerful families, creating enmity [?]. Among those serving in the provincial administration and surveillance commissions, prefectures, and counties, there surely are ministers who spread imperial beneficence and foster harmony. Yet there are also some who exploit the people to enrich themselves and accumulate resentment against the state. Among those charged with protection and defense, there surely are ministers who pledge themselves to the state and will die rather than retreat. Yet there are also some who are craven and inactive, intent only on preserving themselves and escaping danger.

Some even privately promote their associates to purchase gratitude, and openly engage in bribery in violation of the law. Outwardly they have the name of serving their sovereign; inwardly they lack the substance of such service. Thus, the responsibilities entrusted to them for administering their allotted spheres may go unfulfilled, their duties of assistance may remain undischarged, and the sincerity with which they have been entrusted with office and accorded generous treatment may be betrayed, so that they fail to bring their service to a worthy conclusion. Your Majesty treats your ministers with such generosity, yet the way those ministers conduct themselves…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
如是其薄是誠有以勦
陛下今日之慮也臣愚以為唐虞之世賢聖滿朝
而不能無四凶則人臣之有邪正固聖世之
所不免而彰善癉惡舉直錯枉在人君之激
揚何如耳未足為有道之累也故嘗觀之以
堯舜之智燭工鯀之奸宜先有以察其情矣
然必試之不可而後已焉盖其罪之未形不
忍以逆料之見而先以絕其將来是聖人以
厚道待天下者也及其情状既明然後加之
以罰而勿貸焉盖不以姑息之恩而廢天下
===
之法是聖人以大義裁天下者也及其典刑
之既正也不以數人之奸而盡疑在廷之臣
盖賢否既殊與奪各異是聖人以至公待天
下物来順應普物而無心者也夫以二聖之
知人萬世仰其哲二聖之官人萬世仰其智
而皆不免於此焉而亦未嘗以此自病焉然
則
陛下又焉得以負慢之臣而遂自歉於知人之哲
能官之智哉臣嘗仰觀
陛下御極以来固亦有一二侮慢之臣間出於其

punctuated: 如是其薄，是誠有以勦陛下今日之慮也。臣愚以為，唐虞之世，賢聖滿朝，而不能無四凶，則人臣之有邪正，固聖世之所不免，而彰善癉惡、舉直錯枉，在人君之激揚何如耳，未足為有道之累也。故嘗觀之，以堯舜之智，燭工鯀之奸，宜先有以察其情矣。然必試之不可而後已焉，盖其罪之未形，不忍以逆料之見而先以絕其將来，是聖人以厚道待天下者也。及其情状既明，然後加之以罰而勿貸焉，盖不以姑息之恩而廢天下之法，是聖人以大義裁天下者也。及其典刑之既正也，不以數人之奸而盡疑在廷之臣，盖賢否既殊，與奪各異，是聖人以至公待天下，物来順應，普物而無心者也。夫以二聖之知人，萬世仰其哲；二聖之官人，萬世仰其智。而皆不免於此焉，而亦未嘗以此自病焉。然則陛下又焉得以負慢之臣，而遂自歉於知人之哲、能官之智哉？臣嘗仰觀陛下御極以来，固亦有一二侮慢之臣間出於其
translation_en:
…is so deficient. This indeed gives cause for Your Majesty’s present concern [?]. In my humble opinion, in the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, worthies and sages filled the court, yet even then the Four Evildoers could not be wholly avoided. Thus, the presence of both wicked and upright ministers is unavoidable even in an age of sage rule. What matters is how the sovereign discourages evil and encourages good, commending virtue and punishing wickedness, raising up the upright and setting aside the crooked. Their presence is insufficient to discredit a well-governed age.

I have reflected on this: with their wisdom, Yao and Shun could see through the treachery of Gonggong and Gun and should have discerned their true dispositions beforehand. Yet they first put them to the test and dismissed them only after they proved unfit. Before their crimes became manifest, the sages could not bear to cut off their future prospects on the strength of anticipatory judgments. This was how the sages treated all under Heaven with generosity. Once the circumstances became clear, however, they imposed punishment without pardon. They did not allow indulgent kindness to nullify the laws of the realm. This was how the sages judged all under Heaven according to great righteousness. Once the prescribed punishments had been duly enforced, they did not suspect every minister at court because of the treachery of a few. Since the worthy and unworthy differed, so too did the granting and withdrawal of favor. This was how the sages treated all under Heaven with the utmost impartiality, responding appropriately to whatever arose and embracing all things without partial intent [?].

For the two sages’ discernment of men, ten thousand generations admire their insight; for their appointment of men to office, ten thousand generations admire their wisdom. Yet neither could avoid such circumstances, nor did they ever regard this as a failing of their own. How, then, can Your Majesty, on account of faithless and disrespectful ministers, come to feel deficient in the insight needed to discern men or the wisdom needed to appoint them to office? I have respectfully observed that, since Your Majesty ascended the throne, there have indeed occasionally appeared one or two insolent and disrespectful ministers among…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
間矣然皆馭之有道而不得終肆其惡則是
容之於始者非不足於明也於精明之中而
存渾厚之體即堯舜試可後已之心也斷之
於終者非不足於恩也於慈愛之中而寓威
克之道即堯舜流放竄殛之法也邇者考核
諸臣第其殿最而去留予奪斷自
聖心誠有以察淑慝之情而明勸懲之典又堯舜
任賢勿貳去邪勿疑之心也夫忠邪誠偽其
情亦至賾也而今有以得其實焉非天下之
至精不足以與於斯也此臣所以仰頌
===
陛下兼照之智也進退予奪其事亦至繁也而今
有以得其當焉非天下之至神不足以與於
斯也此臣所以仰頌
陛下總攬之權也然則知人官人之道無出於此
矣
陛下乃猶不自滿假而以知能之方下詢臣等臣

…among them. Yet all have been governed by appropriate means and have been unable to give lasting rein to their wickedness. Thus, Your Majesty’s tolerating them at first did not reflect any lack of discernment. Preserving magnanimity amid penetrating clarity is precisely the spirit in which Yao and Shun tested men’s fitness before settling their appointments. Nor did Your Majesty’s decisive action in the end reflect any lack of benevolence. Incorporating the power of stern authority within compassionate care is precisely the method by which Yao and Shun banished, exiled, expelled, and executed offenders. Recently, you assessed your ministers and ranked their performance from worst to best; decisions to dismiss or retain them, grant or withdraw rewards, proceeded from your sagely mind. This has indeed enabled you to discern goodness and wickedness and make clear the rules of encouragement and punishment. This, too, is the spirit of Yao and Shun: employ the worthy without wavering and remove the wicked without hesitation. Loyalty and treachery, sincerity and falsehood are profoundly intricate in their workings, yet you now have the means to ascertain their reality. Only the utmost discernment under Heaven could accomplish this. This is why your servant reverently praises Your Majesty’s all-embracing wisdom. Promotion and demotion, granting and withholding, are exceedingly complex matters, yet you now have the means to handle them fittingly. Only the utmost spiritual acuity under Heaven could accomplish this. This is why your servant reverently praises Your Majesty’s comprehensive command of authority. The way to understand men and appoint them to office goes no further than this.

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
盡善則所以司風教者可辨也財賦之未盡
充則所以司會計者可辨也夷狄之未盡弭
則所以司安攘者可辨也盖天下之事有其
實必有其形即其形而推其實則雖天下之
廣羣情之賾若難於周知焉者而秉吾昭融
之識自將明見於萬里之外若懸鑑以照物
我無與焉而物之妍媸咸莫得而遁焉者矣
官人之道亦不必求之總攬之外也即今日
之總攬者而不已其運焉勵賞罰之典祛因
習之弊德足以熙百工則度德而居之位可
===
也而位浮於德深以負吾之付託者則疏黜
之威所弗惜也才足以康庶事則量才而授
之官可也而才不稱事深以孤吾之任使者
則廢置之法所弗貸也盖天下之事貴其實
不貴其名循其名而責其實則雖任有小大
事有重輕若難於兼總焉者而操吾張弛之
柄自能獨裁於萬化之原若省括以發機其
權在我而勢之疾徐人莫得而與焉者矣夫
智以辨之於始固所以開振作之基而智非
務察之謂也憲天之所以聰明者而已矣權

盡善，則所以司風教者可辨也；財賦之未盡充，則所以司會計者可辨也；夷狄之未盡弭，則所以司安攘者可辨也。盖天下之事，有其實必有其形，即其形而推其實，則雖天下之廣、羣情之賾，若難於周知焉者，而秉吾昭融之識，自將明見於萬里之外，若懸鑑以照物，我無與焉，而物之妍媸咸莫得而遁焉者矣。
官人之道，亦不必求之總攬之外也。即今日之總攬者，而不已其運焉，勵賞罰之典，祛因習之弊。德足以熙百工，則度德而居之位可也；而位浮於德，深以負吾之付託者，則疏黜之威所弗惜也。才足以康庶事，則量才而授之官可也；而才不稱事，深以孤吾之任使者，則廢置之法所弗貸也。盖天下之事，貴其實，不貴其名。循其名而責其實，則雖任有小大、事有重輕，若難於兼總焉者，而操吾張弛之柄，自能獨裁於萬化之原，若省括以發機，其權在我，而勢之疾徐，人莫得而與焉者矣。

translation_en:
…not yet wholly good, then those responsible for moral instruction can be assessed; where revenues are not yet sufficient, those responsible for fiscal accounting can be assessed; where the foreign peoples have not yet been pacified, those responsible for securing the realm and repelling outsiders can be assessed. For every affair under Heaven has an underlying reality that necessarily manifests itself outwardly. By examining its outward manifestation and inferring its underlying reality, even though the vastness of the realm and the intricacy of human dispositions may seem difficult to comprehend fully, one need only maintain one’s clear and penetrating discernment to see distinctly ten thousand li away. It is like suspending a mirror to reflect things: without any intervention on one’s part, nothing beautiful or ugly can escape being revealed.
The way to appoint officials likewise need not be sought beyond the comprehensive control Your Majesty already exercises. Simply continue exercising that control without cease, enforce the established rules of reward and punishment, and eliminate the abuses of habitual practice. If a man’s virtue suffices to bring distinction to the hundred offices, assess his virtue and place him in an appropriate position. But if his position exceeds his virtue and he gravely betrays the trust placed in him, do not hesitate to wield the authority to remove and dismiss him. If his ability suffices to put the many affairs of government in order, gauge his ability and grant him an office. But if his ability does not match his duties and he gravely disappoints the expectations behind his appointment, do not exempt him from the rules governing dismissal. For in the affairs of the realm, substance is prized, not mere name. Follow the name and demand the corresponding substance: even though responsibilities differ in scope and affairs in importance, and may seem difficult to oversee together, by holding the power to tighten and relax control, one can decide alone at the source of all transformations. It is like inspecting an arrow’s nock before releasing the trigger [?]: control rests with oneself, and no one else can intervene in determining the speed or slowness of its momentum.
Now, using wisdom to distinguish men at the outset certainly lays the foundation for vigorous action. Yet wisdom does not mean striving to scrutinize every detail; it means simply taking Heaven’s perceptiveness as one’s model. Authority…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
以勵之於後固所以致明照之實而權非尚
威之謂也體天之所以剛健者而已矣天之
聰明未嘗徧物以求其情而天下自無遺照
天之剛健未嘗徧物以求其當而天下自無
遺化者何哉易簡而天下之理得也今
陛下之諸臣雖曰未能盡體
陛下之意也既已鑒別而黜罰之矣而凡兹簡任
之臣所以推心置其腹者猶昔也則滌德勵
行革薄從忠者將愈奮發而不可懈矣由是
任忠良以為股肱廣言路以為耳目使各悉
===
其聰明條天下之賢否得失而陳之
陛下時總其上計而斟酌焉則臣工之不狃於習
者即
陛下兼照之智也古帝王之所以流言不惑讒間
莫行而四海九州之遠物無遁情者此其要
也使各綜其名實條天下之功罪利害而上
之

者即

punctuated:

今陛下之諸臣，雖曰未能盡體陛下之意也，既已鑒別而黜罰之矣。而凡兹簡任之臣，所以推心置其腹者猶昔也，則滌德勵行、革薄從忠者，將愈奮發而不可懈矣。由是任忠良以為股肱，廣言路以為耳目，使各悉其聰明，條天下之賢否得失而陳之。陛下時總其上計而斟酌焉，則臣工之不狃於習者，即陛下兼照之智也。古帝王之所以流言不惑、讒間莫行，而四海九州之遠，物無遁情者，此其要也。使各綜其名實，條天下之功罪利害而上之。陛下時總其要會而誅賞焉，則臣工之各貞其度者，即陛下總攬之權也。古帝王之所以禁不厲、刑不煩
translation_en:
…to spur them on afterward is indeed how the substance of discerning oversight is achieved. Yet authority does not mean prizing intimidation; it means simply embodying Heaven’s strength and vigor. Heaven’s discernment does not seek out the circumstances of every individual thing, yet nothing under Heaven escapes its illumination. Heaven’s strength and vigor do not seek out what is fitting for every individual thing, yet nothing under Heaven escapes its transforming influence. Why is this? Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped.
Now, although Your Majesty’s ministers may not fully embody Your Majesty’s intentions, you have already distinguished among them and dismissed or punished those at fault. Yet toward all those selected for appointment, you continue as before to entrust your very heart to them. Thus those who cleanse their virtue and strengthen their conduct, abandoning frivolity for loyalty, will become still more zealous and will not slacken. Accordingly, appoint the loyal and worthy as your arms and legs, and broaden the channels of counsel to serve as your ears and eyes. Have each fully exercise his discernment, setting out the worthiness and unworthiness of men and the successes and failures of affairs throughout the realm, and presenting these to you. If Your Majesty periodically brings together and weighs their submitted reports, your officials’ freedom from the constraints of habitual practice will itself constitute Your Majesty’s all-embracing discernment. This was the essential means by which the emperors and kings of antiquity remained undeluded by rumors and impervious to divisive slander, so that even in the distant reaches of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, nothing could conceal its true circumstances.
Have each compare nominal responsibilities with actual performance, setting out accomplishments and offenses, benefits and harms throughout the realm, and submitting them to you. If Your Majesty periodically brings together the essential summaries and administers punishments and rewards, your officials’ steadfast adherence to their proper standards will itself constitute Your Majesty’s comprehensive authority. This was how the emperors and kings of antiquity ensured that prohibitions were not harsh and punishments were not excessive…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
而百司庶府之臣奔走不暇者此其道也故
堯舜之聖所疇咨者惟岳牧諸賢二聖特恭
巳以聽之而靜言庸違者不能爲之眩巧言
令色孔壬者不能爲之移雖有工鯀終不能
病唐虞之治堯舜誠得其道握其要也今
陛下以堯舜之道待其臣則雖諸臣之中或未能
盡以堯舜之臣自待固無損於明良喜起之
盛也
陛下亦惟始終是心而巳何必縁此而遂勞於制
馭耶抑臣嘗聞之先民曰誠精故明則知誠
===
者明之本也今
陛下敬一有箴五箴有註
嚴恭寅畏之念貫徹於
昊穹緝熈敬止之學無間於瞬息即古帝王之誠
敬不越是矣又嘗聞之先民曰明通公溥則
知公者權之用也今
陛下用人惟賢左右惟人大小遠近之任悉决於
神衷進退低昂之機動裁於
天鑒即古帝王之公溥不越是矣夫是以虛靈洞
徹而上下之情狀以明正大高明而天下之

…and this is the way by which the officials of the hundred offices and numerous departments are kept constantly busy in service. Thus, sage though Yao and Shun were, those whom they consulted were the worthy men serving as the Four Peaks and regional governors. The two sages simply held themselves reverently and listened to them. Those whose words were pleasing but whose actions were contrary could not bewilder them; those with clever words and ingratiating looks, deeply deceitful, could not sway them. Even with Gonggong and Gun present, these men ultimately could not impair the governance of Tang and Yu. Yao and Shun truly possessed the right way and grasped its essentials. Now, if Your Majesty treats your ministers according to the way of Yao and Shun, then even if some among them cannot fully hold themselves to the standard of Yao’s and Shun’s ministers, this will surely not diminish the flourishing harmony in which an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers joyfully spur one another to action. Your Majesty need only maintain this same heart from beginning to end. Why, on this account, go so far as to weary yourself with controlling them?
Your servant has also heard this saying of the ancients: “Sincerity, when refined, brings illumination.” Thus we know that sincerity is the foundation of illumination. Now Your Majesty has composed an Admonition on Reverent Unity and commentaries on the Five Admonitions. Your thoughts of solemn reverence and vigilant awe reach to the vast heavens; your cultivation of ever-brightening virtue and abiding reverence never lapses for an instant. Even the sincerity and reverence of the ancient emperors and kings did not surpass this. Your servant has also heard this saying of the ancients: “Illumination penetrates; impartiality extends everywhere.” Thus we know that impartiality is what gives authority its efficacy. Now Your Majesty employs only the worthy and keeps only fitting men at your side. Appointments to great and small posts, near and far, are all decided within your sagely heart; decisions concerning advancement and dismissal, elevation and demotion, are invariably determined by your heavenly discernment. Even the far-reaching impartiality of the ancient emperors and kings did not surpass this. Hence, through your mind’s receptiveness, spiritual acuity, and penetrating clarity, the circumstances of those above and below become manifest; through your uprightness, magnanimity, loftiness, and illumination, the hearts of all under Heaven…

text:
心志以慰臣民

text:
臣金達
臣對臣聞帝王之御天下也必盡官人之道
而後可以致天下之治必得官人之要而後
可以享天下之逸天下之治天下之人為之
也任用弗當則所以輔理承化者無其託而
治功之隳恒必由之何以致雍熈悠久之化
天下之賢天下之相舉之也選擇弗精則所
以崇信任使者非其才而庶績之凝無以致
之何以成人君任人之逸故求賢以弘化者
君之事也而代君以舉賢者相之職也君能
===
其事臣舉其職則天下之事日就於理而官
人之效有可臻無為之治坐享其成而求賢
之勞有所代矣否則以一人之聰明而欲周
知天下之賢則君之明必有所難徧非所以
言官人也况其勞不容已乎以一己之私見
而欲上答求賢之君則相之職必有所難盡
非所以言事君也况其責不可諉乎是故明
主勞于求賢而逸于任人任人者任相是也
一相得而萬國理矣相臣易于事君而艱于
舉人舉人者舉賢是也眾賢輔而百工敘矣

punctuated:
臣金達。

臣對：臣聞帝王之御天下也，必盡官人之道，而後可以致天下之治；必得官人之要，而後可以享天下之逸。天下之治，天下之人為之也。任用弗當，則所以輔理承化者無其託，而治功之隳恒必由之，何以致雍熈悠久之化？天下之賢，天下之相舉之也。選擇弗精，則所以崇信任使者非其才，而庶績之凝無以致之，何以成人君任人之逸？故求賢以弘化者，君之事也；而代君以舉賢者，相之職也。君能其事，臣舉其職，則天下之事日就於理，而官人之效有可臻，無為之治坐享其成，而求賢之勞有所代矣。否則，以一人之聰明而欲周知天下之賢，則君之明必有所難徧，非所以言官人也，况其勞不容已乎？以一己之私見而欲上答求賢之君，則相之職必有所難盡，非所以言事君也，况其責不可諉乎？是故明主勞于求賢，而逸于任人。任人者，任相是也，一相得而萬國理矣。相臣易于事君，而艱于舉人。舉人者，舉賢是也，眾賢輔而百工敘矣。
translation_en:
Your servant, Jin Da.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, in governing All under Heaven, emperors and kings must fully practice the way of appointing officials before they can bring order to the realm; they must grasp the essentials of appointing officials before they can enjoy ease in ruling it. Order in the realm is achieved by the people of the realm. If appointments are inappropriate, there is no one to entrust with assisting governance and carrying forward the ruler’s transforming influence, and the collapse of achievements in government invariably follows from this. How, then, can harmonious, flourishing, and enduring transformation be achieved? The worthy men of the realm are recommended by its chief ministers. If selection is insufficiently discerning, those accorded esteem and trust and entrusted with service will lack the requisite abilities, and there will be no means of bringing the many undertakings of government to fruition. How, then, can the ruler attain the ease that comes from employing others? Thus, seeking worthy men to extend the transforming influence of government is the ruler’s business; recommending worthy men on the ruler’s behalf is the chief minister’s duty. If the ruler performs his task capably and the minister fulfills his office, the affairs of the realm will daily become more orderly, and the benefits of appointing officials can be attained. The ruler can enjoy the accomplishments of government through nonaction, with someone taking his place in the labor of seeking worthy men.

Otherwise, if he wishes, through the intelligence of one person alone, to know all the worthy men in the realm, the ruler’s discernment will inevitably have difficulty reaching everywhere. This is no proper way to speak of appointing officials; moreover, how could his labors ever cease? If a chief minister wishes, through his own private judgment alone, to answer the ruler’s quest for worthy men, he will inevitably find it difficult to fulfill his office completely. This is no proper way to speak of serving the ruler; moreover, how could he shift his responsibility onto others? Therefore, an enlightened ruler labors in seeking worthy men but finds ease in employing others. Employing others means appointing a chief minister: once the right chief minister is found, the myriad states are brought into order. For the chief minister, serving the ruler is easy, but recommending men is difficult. Recommending men means recommending the worthy: when the many worthy men lend their assistance, all the offices are duly ordered.

translation_en:
…among those granted an audience to reply, how could I dare not lay bare my sincere thoughts, to requite even a ten-thousandth part of Your gracious command? Your servant has examined this in the Book of Documents, which says: “Heaven aids the people below, making rulers and teachers for them, that they may assist the Lord on High and cherish and pacify the four quarters.” Thus the ruler is established by Heaven as lord of the people, and it is upon him that the people depend for their well-being. It also says: “Ministers serve as my limbs, ears, and eyes. If I err, correct me. Do not comply to my face and then speak against me after withdrawing. Be reverent, you who stand about me.” Thus ministers are those upon whom the ruler relies as his close advisers, and upon whom the state places its trust. If the ruler wishes to find men through whom to care for the people, he must possess the discernment to understand men and the wisdom to appoint capable officials. Only then will his discrimination be exact, and he will naturally obtain worthy men advancing together into service. If ministers wish to care for the people on their ruler’s behalf, they must fulfill the way of assisting him and exert themselves with selfless devotion. Only then will they remain loyal and steadfast, and naturally fulfill their responsibility to bring his work to completion on his behalf.

If the ruler does not understand men, the worthy and unworthy will be mixed together without distinction, and the loyal and the wicked will advance side by side without scrutiny. His beneficence will fail to reach those below, and it will be difficult to expect him to care for the people. If ministers fail to discharge their duties, they will betray what the ruler has entrusted to them and fail to achieve the results he demands. If they have not fully exerted their minds and strength, it would be false to call them loyal. Yet Heaven’s work is performed by men: an office is established for each task. To bring the ruler’s work to completion on his behalf, the many affairs of government are apportioned among the many officials. The duties and responsibilities are therefore too numerous to enumerate exhaustively, while differences in wisdom and folly cannot be made uniform. Dwelling within the ninefold palace enclosure and burdened with the myriad concerns of government, how could the ruler select every individual with precision and employ every individual appropriately? 又在官矣故堯之憂憂不得乎舜而已舜之
外無憂也舜之時非無比周為黨者也而所
任者禹臯陶也禹臯得而羣哲勉輔矣故舜
之憂憂不得乎禹臯而已禹臯之外無憂也
堯惟得舜以分之治故治水成績者舜舉之
也明刑弼教者舜舉之也典禮典樂者舜舉
之也亮采惠疇之有人而於變時雍之治成
堯其獨勞于上乎舜惟得禹臯以分之治故
九德咸事者禹臯率之也百僚師師者禹臯
率之也四隣之欽哉禹臯率之也宅揆秉衡

乎君明臣良而相得者益章君逸臣勞而相

三代之隆亦知此道故其治功後世不可幾

非無側席求賢之君然不知任相之逸者其
勞不足尚也下非無為君求賢之相然不知
求賢之公者其私不可訓也世道日趨於汚

…the able men [?] were in office. Thus Yao’s sole concern was that he might not obtain Shun’s service; beyond Shun, he had no concern. In Shun’s time, there were certainly men who colluded and formed factions, but those he entrusted with office were Yu and Gao Yao. Once Yu and Gao Yao were secured, all the wise men diligently assisted. Thus Shun’s sole concern was that he might not obtain the services of Yu and Gao Yao; beyond them, he had no concern.

Yao secured Shun to share the work of government. Those who achieved success in controlling the waters were therefore men whom Shun had recommended; those who clarified punishments to support moral instruction were men whom Shun had recommended; and those who directed ritual and music were men whom Shun had recommended. With men available to discharge their duties faithfully and order the various affairs, government brought about a transformation into harmony. Did Yao, then, toil alone above them? Shun secured Yu and Gao Yao to share the work of government. Thus it was they who led those possessing the nine virtues to serve in office; they who led the hundred officials to learn from one another; and they who led the attendants on every side to act with reverence. With men available to direct affairs and hold the balance of government, the splendid influence that stirred the four quarters like the wind became manifest. Did Shun, then, toil alone above them?

When the ruler was enlightened and his ministers worthy, their mutual accord shone ever more brightly; when the ruler was at ease and his ministers labored, their mutual dependence brought affairs to completion. Such was the government of Tang and Yu: how exalted, beyond surpassing! At the height of the Three Dynasties, rulers likewise understood this way. Thus their achievements in government were beyond the reach of later ages, and even the flourishing government of Tang and Yu did not surpass them. Thereafter, from the Han down to the Song, there was no lack of rulers above who shifted upon their seats in eager anticipation of worthy men. Yet those who did not understand the ease afforded by entrusting government to chief ministers undertook labors unworthy of esteem. Below, there was no lack of chief ministers who sought worthy men for their rulers. Yet those who did not understand impartiality in seeking worthy men displayed a partiality that could not serve as a model. As the ways of the world grew daily more corrupt and the court’s transforming governance failed to flourish, why should one wonder that this was so?

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
聰明天賦
睿知夙成屢下敷求之
詔而在野無遺賢時舉考核之
典而在位無比德大小臣工固宜攄悃輸忠鞠
躬盡瘁以圖報千萬一則
天地所以覆我載我之仁
大君所以生我成我之恩庶乎知所酬矣何敢忘
其所自而有仇讎之視也孟子曰君之視臣
如手足則臣視君如腹心況乎君以心腹置
臣腹中而臣以仇讎視之則莫大之罪無所
===
逃於人怒誰其能逭之哉然人心不同賢不
肖相去不能一律齊也是故有輔弼論思之
臣焉秉忠竭誠者固多而阿比逢迎者或有
也有臺省藩臬之臣焉精白承休者固多而
誣上行私者或有也有邊鄙將校之臣焉宣
力効死者固多而觀望退縮者或有也有州
邑牧圉之臣焉奉公守法者固多而營身肥
家者或有也若是者豈
陛下知人之哲能官之智有不足耶
天有大明而日月之所不及不損其為明

聰明天賦，睿知夙成，屢下敷求之詔，而在野無遺賢；時舉考核之典，而在位無比德。大小臣工固宜攄悃輸忠，鞠躬盡瘁，以圖報千萬一，則天地所以覆我載我之仁，大君所以生我成我之恩，庶乎知所酬矣。何敢忘其所自，而有仇讎之視也？孟子曰：「君之視臣如手足，則臣視君如腹心。」況乎君以心腹置臣腹中，而臣以仇讎視之，則莫大之罪無所逃於人怒，誰其能逭之哉？
然人心不同，賢不肖相去，不能一律齊也。是故有輔弼論思之臣焉，秉忠竭誠者固多，而阿比逢迎者或有也；有臺省藩臬之臣焉，精白承休者固多，而誣上行私者或有也；有邊鄙將校之臣焉，宣力効死者固多，而觀望退縮者或有也；有州邑牧圉之臣焉，奉公守法者固多，而營身肥家者或有也。若是者，豈陛下知人之哲、能官之智有不足耶？天有大明，而日月之所不及，不損其為明。
translation_en:
…endowed by Heaven with intelligence, your sagacious understanding matured early. You have repeatedly issued edicts seeking worthy men far and wide, so that no worthy man outside office remains overlooked; you have regularly instituted performance evaluations, so that those in office do not collude in wrongdoing. Officials great and small should surely lay bare their sincerity and offer their loyalty, bending themselves to their duties and exhausting their strength, in the hope of repaying even one ten-millionth of what they owe. Only then might they be said to understand how to repay the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, which shelter and sustain us, and the grace of the great sovereign, who nurtures us and brings us to fulfillment. How dare they forget the source of these blessings and regard their ruler as an enemy? Mengzi said: “When the ruler regards his ministers as his hands and feet, the ministers regard their ruler as their belly and heart.” How much worse, then, when the ruler places his own heart within his ministers’ bellies, yet they regard him as an enemy! Such an enormous crime cannot escape the wrath of others. Who could evade it?
Yet people’s hearts differ, and the worthy and unworthy stand far apart: they cannot all be brought into conformity with a single standard. Thus, among ministers who assist the ruler and deliberate on affairs, many indeed maintain loyalty and exert their utmost sincerity, yet some form cliques and flatter. Among officials of the Censorate and central ministries, and of the provincial administration and surveillance commissions, many indeed receive your beneficence with pure and unsullied devotion, yet some deceive their superiors and pursue private interests. Among commanders and officers on the frontiers, many indeed exert their strength and give their lives in service, yet some wait to see how matters develop and shrink back. Among officials who shepherd and safeguard the people in prefectures and counties, many indeed serve the public and uphold the law, yet some seek their own advantage and enrich their families. Do such cases mean that Your Majesty’s discernment in judging men and wisdom in assigning them to office are deficient? Heaven possesses great brightness, and the places that the sun and moon do not reach do not diminish that brightness.…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
君有大智而耳目之所未周不害其爲智然則今
之所謂不法不廉以仇讎視者是亦血氣之
類作孽尊以自速戾于厥躬耳于
陛下何累哉亦惟察之以明知其不可原也則因
其情而按之不以人言而失之縱秉之以公
知其不可宥也則因其罪而誅之不以姑息
而失之寬主之以斷知其不可容釋也則因
其不才而黜逐之不以因循而失之緩一刑
之施明如日月而天下咸知其當一罪之加
威如雷霆而天下咸懼其威又奚臣工之敢
===
不自盡其忠哉雖然此則因其罪而言之耳
陛下猶欲聞知能之方而謂臣等有懷知能之道
俾臣勿諱勿欺臣竊謂有所爲而不言諱也
有所言而不盡欺也臣於平日以此自戒久
矣而况第一進言之始敢蹈是咎而不以官
人之要爲
陛下悉陳之哉臣謂臣者分君之治以爲治者也
相者統臣之職以爲職者也君不得臣固不
足以弘化而君不擇相又不可以得人故相
者君所任以知人求賢而措天下國家于寧

君有大智，而耳目之所未周，不害其爲智。然則今之所謂不法不廉、以仇讎視者，是亦血氣之類，作孽尊以自速戾于厥躬耳，于陛下何累哉？亦惟察之以明，知其不可原也，則因其情而按之，不以人言而失之縱；秉之以公，知其不可宥也，則因其罪而誅之，不以姑息而失之寬；主之以斷，知其不可容釋也，則因其不才而黜逐之，不以因循而失之緩。一刑之施，明如日月，而天下咸知其當；一罪之加，威如雷霆，而天下咸懼其威，又奚臣工之敢不自盡其忠哉？

雖然，此則因其罪而言之耳。陛下猶欲聞知能之方，而謂臣等有懷知能之道，俾臣勿諱勿欺。臣竊謂有所爲而不言，諱也；有所言而不盡，欺也。臣於平日以此自戒久矣，而况第一進言之始，敢蹈是咎，而不以官人之要爲陛下悉陳之哉？臣謂臣者，分君之治以爲治者也；相者，統臣之職以爲職者也。君不得臣，固不足以弘化；而君不擇相，又不可以得人。故相者，君所任以知人求賢，而措天下國家于寧
translation_en:
…A ruler possesses great wisdom; that his eyes and ears do not reach everywhere does not diminish that wisdom. Thus those now described as lawless and corrupt, and regarded as enemies, are also creatures of flesh and blood: by committing wrongdoing [?], they merely hasten the arrival of guilt upon themselves. How could they bring discredit upon Your Majesty? Only scrutinize them discerningly: when you know that they cannot be excused, investigate them according to the circumstances of their conduct, and do not err by letting them off on the strength of what others say. Deal with them impartially: when you know that they cannot be pardoned, punish them according to their offenses, and do not err through indulgent leniency. Preside over their cases decisively: when you know that they cannot be tolerated or released, dismiss and expel them for their unfitness, and do not err through habitual procrastination. Let the imposition of each punishment be as clear as the sun and moon, so that all under Heaven recognize its justice; let the punishment of each offense be as awe-inspiring as thunder, so that all under Heaven fear its power. Then how would any official dare fail to give his utmost loyalty?

Nevertheless, this speaks only of their offenses. Your Majesty still wishes to hear methods for discerning men and appointing them to office, and says that we may harbor knowledge of the way to do so, instructing your servant neither to conceal nor to deceive. Your servant humbly considers that to leave unspoken something that has been done is concealment; to speak without telling everything is deception. I have long cautioned myself against these things in daily life. How much less, on this first occasion of offering counsel, would I dare incur such blame by failing to lay fully before Your Majesty the essentials of appointing men to office? Your servant holds that ministers administer a share of the ruler’s government, while the chief councilor’s duty is to coordinate the duties of the ministers. If the ruler does not obtain suitable ministers, he certainly cannot extend his transforming influence; yet if he does not choose his chief councilor carefully, neither can he obtain the right men. Thus the chief councilor is the one whom the ruler entrusts with discerning men and seeking the worthy, and with bringing all under Heaven, the state, and the ruling house into tranquility…

text:
謐者也是故善官人者任相而已矣必相之
得而後君之知有所不及者相代以知之善
任相者推心而已矣必心之推而後相之責
有不可辭者始有以盡之故夫君之於相也
真知灼見于其先則相之代君以求賢者必
非狥私阿黨者矣委任責成于其後則相之
以人而事君者必非惟爾不任者矣是故為
君求輔弼論思之臣也而阿附逢迎者弗之
舉矣為君求臺省藩臬之臣也而誣上行私
者弗之舉矣為君求邊鄙將校之臣也而觀
===
望退縮者弗之舉矣為君求州邑牧圉之臣
也而營身肥家者弗之舉矣由是而輔弼論
思之臣得則所以論道經邦啓心沃心者不
有人乎臺省藩臬之臣得則所以激濁揚清
宣旬布惠者不有人乎邊鄙將校之臣得則
所以干城敵愾攘夷却狄者不有人乎州邑
牧圉之臣得則所以撫字保障生養蕃息者
不有人乎人君者元首也所以為之股肱耳
目者惟令之從而無所違惟職之共而無所
惰則可以中天下而立澤四海之民如天之

punctuated: 謐者也。是故善官人者，任相而已矣。必相之得，而後君之知有所不及者，相代以知之。善任相者，推心而已矣。必心之推，而後相之責有不可辭者，始有以盡之。故夫君之於相也，真知灼見于其先，則相之代君以求賢者，必非狥私阿黨者矣；委任責成于其後，則相之以人而事君者，必非惟爾不任者矣。是故為君求輔弼論思之臣也，而阿附逢迎者弗之舉矣；為君求臺省藩臬之臣也，而誣上行私者弗之舉矣；為君求邊鄙將校之臣也，而觀望退縮者弗之舉矣；為君求州邑牧圉之臣也，而營身肥家者弗之舉矣。由是而輔弼論思之臣得，則所以論道經邦、啓心沃心者，不有人乎？臺省藩臬之臣得，則所以激濁揚清、宣旬布惠者，不有人乎？邊鄙將校之臣得，則所以干城敵愾、攘夷却狄者，不有人乎？州邑牧圉之臣得，則所以撫字保障、生養蕃息者，不有人乎？人君者，元首也。所以為之股肱耳目者，惟令之從而無所違，惟職之共而無所惰，則可以中天下而立，澤四海之民，如天之
translation_en:
…tranquillity. Thus, a ruler skilled in appointing officials need only appoint the right chief minister. Only when the right chief minister has been secured can he supply the discernment that lies beyond the ruler’s own knowledge. To employ a chief minister well requires only that the ruler give him his wholehearted trust. Only once that trust has been extended can the chief minister fully discharge the responsibilities he cannot decline. Thus, in dealing with his chief minister, if the ruler first knows him truly and judges him clearly, the minister who seeks worthy men on the ruler’s behalf will assuredly not indulge private interests or favor factions. If the ruler then entrusts him with authority and holds him accountable for results, the minister who serves the ruler by supplying capable men will assuredly not fail to shoulder that charge [?].

Thus, when seeking ministers to assist the ruler and deliberate on affairs, he will not recommend flatterers and sycophants. When seeking officials for the Censorate, central administrative agencies, and provincial administration and surveillance commissions, he will not recommend those who deceive their superiors and pursue private interests. When seeking commanders and officers for the frontiers, he will not recommend those who hesitate and shrink back. When seeking officials to shepherd and protect the people of the subprefectures and counties, he will not recommend those who advance themselves and enrich their households.

Once the right ministers have been secured to assist and deliberate, will there not be men to discuss the Way, order the state, and enlighten and nourish the ruler’s mind? Once the right officials have been secured for the Censorate, central agencies, and provincial commissions, will there not be men to curb corruption, promote integrity, proclaim instruction [?], and distribute benefits? Once the right frontier commanders and officers have been secured, will there not be men to serve as shields and ramparts, confront the enemy’s hostility, and repel the Yi and Di peoples? Once the right officials have been secured to shepherd and protect the subprefectures and counties, will there not be men to nurture and safeguard the people, sustain their livelihoods, and enable them to flourish and multiply?

The ruler is the head. If those who serve as his limbs, ears, and eyes obey his commands without contravention and attend to their duties without negligence, he can stand at the center of all under Heaven and bestow blessings upon the people within the Four Seas, just as Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
運行于上而四時之吏五行之佐為之宣其
氣矣君不可以自逸也耶若曰人人而欲擇
之精官之當似有失於大君之體而日見其
叢脞矣雖勞奚益也是故君不可以不逸逸
者逸于任相也相不可以不勞勞者勞于求
賢也知勞逸之有其分則知官人之有其要
矣雖然
陛下知能之道臣固以為在擇相矣然相之所當
自盡者又何如哉必思曰相者君股肱耳目
之所寄也使於心有不盡君之望我者何如
===
而可如此也必于四門則闢之凡可以得賢
者無不為之圖于側陋則揚之凡所以官人
者無不得其當始之以甄别之明而網羅之
收采必精也參之以舉用之公而私門之桃
李弗植也或舉于親雖親而在所不避或舉
于仇雖怨而有所不恤則庶乎可以成君知
人之智而安民之仁亦舉之矣皐陶曰知人
則哲能官人安民則惠黎民懷之能哲而惠
何憂乎驩兜何遷乎有苗何畏乎巧言令色
孔壬然則官人之要非臣之所望於

何憂乎驩兜何遷乎有苗何畏乎巧言令色
孔壬然則官人之要非臣之所望於
punctuated:
運行于上，而四時之吏、五行之佐為之宣其氣矣。君不可以自逸也耶？若曰人人而欲擇之精、官之當，似有失於大君之體，而日見其叢脞矣，雖勞奚益也？是故君不可以不逸，逸者逸于任相也；相不可以不勞，勞者勞于求賢也。知勞逸之有其分，則知官人之有其要矣。
雖然，陛下知能之道，臣固以為在擇相矣。然相之所當自盡者，又何如哉？必思曰：「相者，君股肱耳目之所寄也。使於心有不盡，君之望我者何如，而可如此也？」必于四門則闢之，凡可以得賢者，無不為之圖；于側陋則揚之，凡所以官人者，無不得其當。始之以甄别之明，而網羅之收采必精也；參之以舉用之公，而私門之桃李弗植也。或舉于親，雖親而在所不避；或舉于仇，雖怨而有所不恤。則庶乎可以成君知人之智，而安民之仁亦舉之矣。
皐陶曰：「知人則哲，能官人；安民則惠，黎民懷之。能哲而惠，何憂乎驩兜？何遷乎有苗？何畏乎巧言令色孔壬？」然則官人之要，非臣之所望於
translation_en:
…moving above, while the officers of the four seasons and the assistants of the five phases disseminate its vital force. May the ruler not then allow himself ease? If he wishes to select every single person with precision and appoint each appropriately, this would seem to detract from the dignity of the great sovereign and increasingly entangle him in petty details. Though he labors, what benefit would there be? Thus the ruler must enjoy ease: his ease lies in entrusting affairs to a chief councilor. The chief councilor must labor: his labor lies in seeking worthy men. Once one understands that labor and ease each have their proper allocation, one understands the essential principle of appointing men to office.
Nevertheless, your servant firmly believes that Your Majesty’s way of recognizing ability [?] lies in choosing a chief councilor. Yet how should the chief councilor exert himself to the utmost? He must reflect: “The chief councilor is entrusted with serving as the ruler’s limbs, ears, and eyes. If I fail to give my whole heart to the task, what of my ruler’s expectations of me? How could I act thus?” He must open the four gates, devising every possible means of obtaining worthy men; he must raise up those in humble obscurity, ensuring that every appointment is appropriate. He must begin with clear discernment in assessing men, so that those gathered into his net are carefully selected. He must complement this with impartiality in recommendation and employment, planting no ‘peach and plum trees’—personal protégés—at his private gate. If he recommends a relative, kinship should not make him refrain; if he recommends an enemy, resentment should not concern him. Thus he may help perfect his ruler’s wisdom in knowing men and also realize the benevolence that brings peace to the people.
Gao Yao said: “To know men is to be discerning, and thus able to appoint men to office; to bring peace to the people is to be beneficent, and the common people cherish such a ruler. If one can be discerning and beneficent, why worry about Huan Dou? Why banish the Youmiao? Why fear those with clever words and ingratiating looks, those great flatterers?” Is not, then, this essential principle of appointing men to office what your servant hopes for from …

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
陛下者哉雖然臣又聞之為政在人取人以身修
身以道修道以仁則人君之身又為取人之
本而況欲擇一相以理萬國奚可不求之于
身也臣願
陛下之持敬也不徒曰郊則恭虔廟嚴孝趨已也
而敬之持也合隱微大小而無間
陛下之主一也不徒曰弗貳以二弗參以三已也
而一之主也合久暫始終而一致如堯之兢
兢如舜之業業如禹之祗台德先如湯之聖
敬日躋如文之亦臨亦保如武之克勘用德
===
涵養此心于未發之先而湛一精明之體不
使其或淆也省察此心于已發之際而不偏
不倚之用不使其或乖也戒聲色貨利以保
養此心親賢人君子以維持此心則藻鑑清
明而私欲莫能以汨之權衡不忒而事物莫
能以撓之殆見相之所擇無有不賢人之所
官無有不當以之照臨百官而阜成兆民則
人無有比德者此也民無有失所者此也放
勳重華之治固可見于
今日而鞏

punctuated:
陛下者哉？雖然，臣又聞之：「為政在人，取人以身，修身以道，修道以仁。」則人君之身，又為取人之本，而況欲擇一相以理萬國，奚可不求之于身也？臣願陛下之持敬也，不徒曰郊則恭虔、廟嚴孝趨已也，而敬之持也，合隱微大小而無間；陛下之主一也，不徒曰弗貳以二、弗參以三已也，而一之主也，合久暫始終而一致。如堯之兢兢，如舜之業業，如禹之祗台德先，如湯之聖敬日躋，如文之亦臨亦保，如武之克勘用德。

涵養此心于未發之先，而湛一精明之體，不使其或淆也；省察此心于已發之際，而不偏不倚之用，不使其或乖也。戒聲色貨利以保養此心，親賢人君子以維持此心，則藻鑑清明，而私欲莫能以汨之；權衡不忒，而事物莫能以撓之。殆見相之所擇無有不賢，人之所官無有不當。以之照臨百官而阜成兆民，則人無有比德者此也，民無有失所者此也。放勳重華之治，固可見于今日，而鞏
translation_en:
…of Your Majesty? Nevertheless, your servant has also heard: “The conduct of government depends upon men; selecting men depends upon one’s own person; cultivating one’s person depends upon the Way; cultivating the Way depends upon benevolence.” Thus the ruler’s own person is the foundation for selecting men. How much more, when seeking a single chief minister to govern the myriad states, must he look to himself? Your servant hopes that Your Majesty’s maintenance of reverence will not consist merely in saying that you are respectful and devout at the suburban sacrifices and solemn and filial in your attendance at the ancestral temple [?]. Rather, may that reverence embrace the hidden and subtle, the great and small, without interruption. May Your Majesty’s concentration upon unity consist not merely in saying that you will not divide your attention between two things or disperse it among three. Rather, may that concentration remain consistent through long and short periods, from beginning to end. Be watchful like Yao and vigilant like Shun; like Yu, reverently place your own virtue first; like Tang, daily advance in sagely reverence; like King Wen, both oversee and protect; and like King Wu, be capable of employing virtue [?].

Nurture this mind before its feelings arise, allowing nothing to confuse its clear, undivided, and luminous substance. Examine this mind when its feelings have arisen, allowing nothing to distort its impartial and balanced functioning. Guard against sensual pleasures and material gain to preserve and nourish this mind; draw close to worthy men and gentlemen to sustain it. Then your mirror of discernment will be clear and bright, and selfish desires will be unable to cloud it; your scales of judgment will be unerring, and affairs and things will be unable to disturb them. We may then expect that every chief minister selected will be worthy and every man appointed to office will be suitably placed. With this, oversee the hundred officials and enrich and perfect the lives of the myriad people. This is how men will be free of factional loyalties, and how none of the people will lack their proper place. The governance of Fangxun and Chonghua—Yao and Shun—can assuredly be witnessed today, and strengthen …

title: 嘉靖三十五年進士登科錄
text:
國祚于苞桑之固措天下于泰山之安臣知其
無窮期矣豈非斯□之大幸哉臣愚鄙猥承
清問俾之盡言故長□其狂瞽及此惟
陛下矜而宥之不勝幸甚臣干冒
天威無任戰慄隕越之至

translation_en:
…the dynasty’s fortunes as firmly as a clump of mulberry trees is rooted, and settle all under Heaven in security as enduring as Mount Tai. Your servant knows that this will have no end. Would this not be a great blessing for this [illegible] [?]!
Your servant, ignorant and uncultivated, has undeservedly received your august inquiry and been permitted to speak fully; hence I have elaborated [?] my rash and benighted words to this extent. May Your Majesty take pity on me and pardon me; I would be exceedingly grateful. Having presumed to affront your heavenly majesty, your servant is overcome with trembling and the utmost fear of falling into ruin.
